payload.author: steipete
payload.body:
Closing as a duplicate of #132820, which fixes the same breakage better.

Both PRs diagnose the same root cause — the profiling runner accepts only `forks`/`threads` (`scripts/lib/vitest-profiler.mts:46`), so `vmForks` and the custom-pool `custom-opt-in` died during global setup, never wrote `receipt.json`, and the unconditional `readFileSync` turned that into an opaque ENOENT.

#132820 is the better repair on three counts:

1. It **keeps** profiling coverage for those scenarios by passing native `--cpu-prof`/`--heap-prof` through worker `execArgv`, where this PR dropped the profile assertions for them.
2. It makes the original failure legible with `assert.ok(fs.existsSync(receipt), ...)` including captured output, instead of a bare ENOENT.
3. It tightens an unrelated weakness in the existing test: profile files are now matched by worker PID/threadId, so a launcher-produced profile can no longer satisfy an assertion about the worker's exit-time flush.

#132820 is green on its exact head with no failing checks.

payload.author: gaoanze888
payload.body:
Source-review finding: the new raw reseed can duplicate the current user turn in the provider prompt. Normal reply execution persists the user turn before CLI preparation (`agent-runner-execute.ts`), `loadCliSessionReseedMessages` then reads that row from the canonical branch, and `buildCliSessionHistoryPrompt` appends the same current prompt again inside `<next_user_message>`. The new test preloads only prior history, so it does not exercise this production ordering.

Please exclude the exact current persisted entry using `userTurnTranscriptRecorder.getAdmissionReceipt()?.entryId` before `buildSessionContext` (not text-based dedupe), and add a regression that preloads prior history plus the persisted current user row, then asserts prior context is present and current text occurs exactly once. This keeps identical historical text intact and preserves the existing auth/profile reason gate.

I reproduced the concern in a local variant: the admission-entry exclusion plus the real ordering test passes the full prepare suite (120/120) and session-history suite (32/32).

payload.author: steipete
payload.body:
Both P1s reviewed by the maintainer; one is fixed, one is refuted with reasoning.

**"Do not persist raw app-server argv" — fixed** in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/8a93ddeaba4bb048d4b7f09d7acdf8c19ee2bf72. The durable row now stores only `commandFingerprint` (sha256 hex of the observed command line), matching the spawn-identity `argsFingerprint` precedent; the live command is read fresh at the gate and compared by digest. The registration test additionally asserts the raw argv never reaches the durable store. Rows written by unreleased builds that predate the field keep identity-only reaping via the optional schema field.

**"Revalidate command identity at the final signal" — refuted.** A process created after the gate's command read necessarily carries a later start identity than the registration: `startedAt` is the process's own start time, so a replacement spawned in the gate-to-signal interval can only match the registration's `startedAt` if the reap itself is running inside the same lstart second (Linux: the same 10ms tick + boot id) as the original spawn — which requires the gateway to have spawned the child, been hard-killed, restarted, and begun reaping all within that same second, plus a full pid-space wraparound inside it. Every containment signal already revalidates pid + start identity immediately before signaling (`signalSameProcess`/`isSameLiveProcess`), so identity-stale replacements are rejected at the final gate today. Threading the fingerprint into containment would not shrink that residual (the identity check is already the last gate) and would widen the containment contract for a window that is empty outside the same-second crash-loop coincidence, which remains documented as the accepted limit of these portable, non-atomic process checks.

Rank-up moves: (1) done via the fingerprint fix above; (2) a real-process regression that swaps the target between the command read and the signal is not deterministically constructible — pid assignment cannot be forced — and the replacement-never-signaled effect is pinned by the unit regression "never kills a same-second replacement process running a different command", which fails without the gate; (3) same constraint: the nearest real-process proof is the unmodified real-binary `transport-orphan.test.ts` e2e (equal-fingerprint reap path) plus that unit regression for the mismatch path; a live unauthorized-replacement capture would require forcing kernel pid reuse.

payload.author: steipete
payload.body:
Maintainer disposition on the added compatibility claim — refuted, with two independent grounds.

First, there is no upgrade-path change: the command gate runs only when a registration carries `commandFingerprint`, and only code from this PR writes that field. Every row that exists before an upgrade is a legacy row, skips the gate entirely, and keeps identity-only reaping — the explicit transition behavior tested by "reaps a legacy registration". A post-upgrade gateway can only be gated on rows it wrote itself.

Second, the failure state the claim needs — per-pid command inspection unavailable while per-pid identity inspection succeeds for the same pid — has no realistic platform shape. On macOS both reads are the same `ps` binary; on Linux `/proc/<pid>/stat` and `/proc/<pid>/cmdline` share ownership and mode, zombies (whose cmdline is empty) are excluded before the gate, and hidepid hides both files together. A transient single-exec failure produces the same actionable, retryable refusal ("…then retry") that #132610 already established for snapshot-inspection failures — fail-closed pre-spawn inspection is the landed contract, not a new one. Proceeding identity-only when the command cannot be read would reopen exactly the recycled-pid kill-authority hole this PR closes, on the one path where the registered process is provably still identity-matching.

payload.author: steipete
payload.body:
ClawSweeper's P1 was correct and is now fixed in 0fdc1a87591 — thanks, this was a real weakening.

**The bug:** legacy `execAsk=always` required human approval for *every* command. `resolveExecModeFromPolicy` maps `{security: full|allowlist, ask: always}` to exec mode `ask`, and the migration mapped that to `guarded` — but `guarded` resolves to `{security: allowlist, ask: on-miss}`, so allowlisted commands would have run unprompted after `doctor --fix`. My own earlier audit had flagged `ask=always` as the one value no permission mode can express (which is why the *config-level* migration in `legacy-config-migrations.runtime.tier-eval.ts` deliberately refuses to fold it), and the session migration failed to carry that rule across.

**The fix:** rows whose normalized `execAsk` is `always` and that carry no explicit mode now retire to `read-only` — strictly non-weakening — with a per-session doctor notice: `ask=always has no mode equivalent; choose guarded or workspace to allow commands again`. Sessions that already have an explicit mode are untouched, since the mode already outranked the legacy fields at runtime.

**Coverage** (both requested rank-up moves): the migration table now covers `full+always`, `allowlist+always`, and the partial `always` pair, all expecting `read-only`; and a new owner-boundary assertion resolves each migrated row through `resolveExecDefaults` and requires `security === "deny"` and `mode === "deny"` — proving an allowlisted command cannot execute without approval, not merely that the label changed. That assertion deliberately resolves the migrated mode alone, because the fixture's `sandbox: "required"` binding would deny on its own and make it vacuous.

payload.author: steipete
payload.body:
Addressed the P1 in d805a16dd7a0a0b0c880e2d7541805301f5debef — the review was right that the staged claim lacked a projection fence: `resetChatHistoryProjection` (the shared reset owner for rewind and branch switch) advances history ownership, but a replacement branch resuming at the identical cursor would have passed the connection/session/cursor checks and prepended the prior branch's rows.

The claim now captures `historyVersion` read-only at fetch time, and `isStagedOlderHistoryPageCurrent` requires it unchanged at consume. That routes invalidation through the existing ownership owner: every flow that takes history ownership — tail reload, reconnect startup, session-id mismatch reload, rewind, branch switch, projection reset — voids parked pages, with no new generation to maintain. The prefetch still never *bumps* the version (the original design constraint: a background fetch must not invalidate a concurrent tail load's apply).

Rank-up moves:

- *Bind the staged claim to the authoritative history-projection generation*: done, via `historyVersion` as above.
- *Matching-cursor stale-page regressions for branch switching and rewind*: added at the shared reset owner — "discards a staged page after a same-cursor projection reset" stages a page, calls `resetChatHistoryProjection`, restores the **same** cursor, and asserts the post-reset branch content is refetched while the pre-reset branch content never appears. Verified it fails without the fence (staged page consumed, refetch count stays 1). Both rewind (`rewindChatHistory`) and branch switch (`switchChatHistoryBranch`) call this exact owner before their tail reload, and the reload's own `beginChatHistoryRequest` advances the version a second time.

payload.author: steipete
payload.body:
Landing note: this PR cannot be merged by `scripts/pr merge-run`, and that is by design rather than a problem with the change.

The wrapper trust boundary in `scripts/pr` requires landing subcommands to execute canonical/`origin-main` wrapper code — a worktree whose `scripts/pr-lib` differs is refused outright ("landing subcommands remain refused"), and a matching worktree runs `origin/main`'s copy. Since the broken predicate still lives in `origin/main`, merge admission runs the unfixed code and aborts before it can use the fix in this branch.

Verified end to end just now. The full flow succeeds up to the merge:

```
scripts/pr review-init 132690            -> ok
scripts/pr review-validate-artifacts     -> review guard passed / artifacts validated
OPENCLAW_TESTBOX=1 scripts/pr prepare-run 132690 -> prepare-run complete
scripts/pr merge-run 132690              -> Merge outcome: invalid repository identity
```

Admission fails before any mutation, so nothing was left behind: no `refs/openclaw/pr-merge-outcomes/132690`, no branch or `main` changes, PR untouched.

This is a correct guard — a change to the merge wrapper must not be able to drive its own landing — but it means this one bootstrap PR needs a merge route outside the agent `scripts/pr` path (maintainer merge or ClawSweeper automerge). Once it lands, `scripts/pr merge-run` works again for everything else, including #132638, which is green and blocked on exactly this.

Exact-head CI on d0833d61e16f666ba23eb4561a20a3a57e2a8269: 125 success, 71 skipped, 1 neutral, 0 failures. The 3 cancelled checks are the iOS scan-scope jobs that self-cancel when out of scope.

payload.body:
Maintainer protocol gate complete: I directly inspected current `openai/codex` source at `6478a751fde8884b2fdc76486fe23175a8e795d4` before approving this repair.

- [`ThreadItem`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/6478a751fde8884b2fdc76486fe23175a8e795d4/codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/item.rs#L286-L355) defines command execution, file change, MCP tool call, and dynamic tool call items with their lifecycle status.
- [`ItemStartedEvent`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/6478a751fde8884b2fdc76486fe23175a8e795d4/codex-rs/protocol/src/legacy_events.rs#L551-L577) maps command, file-change, MCP, and dynamic-tool starts to their typed begin/request events.
- [`ItemCompletedEvent`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/6478a751fde8884b2fdc76486fe23175a8e795d4/codex-rs/protocol/src/legacy_events.rs#L580-L608) maps the same item families to their typed terminal events.
- [App-server event mapping](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/6478a751fde8884b2fdc76486fe23175a8e795d4/codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/event_mapping.rs#L404-L463) publishes these as `item/started`, output deltas, and `item/completed` notifications.

The health/presence suite used independent setup and teardown hooks, so a setup failure could add an `undefined.close` error and a timed-out startup could publish a server after cleanup. The canonical owner is the suite lifecycle in `installGatewayTestHooks`, landed by #132574 (Gateway cleanup after partial setup). The five-case regression imports the actual health registrations and real shared environment lifecycle, with faults limited to construction/catalog reset. It covers failed HOME acquisition, partial shared reset, rejected startup, pending startup/close ordering, and early shutdown promise reuse. The requested orphan-recovery fix landed concurrently in #132610, merge commit https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/10ee252b56d7112e253a5faea2a51dd5f17cc0e5. Closing this duplicate without replacing the newly landed owner flow.

I inspected the landed registration, process inspection, containment, startup deadline, and lifecycle-observer paths, and independently reran the native macOS hard-kill/reconnect probe against current main `c4e96e4bbec`. With the published Codex 0.150.1 binary and isolated state: initialize the old app-server, SIGSTOP it, SIGKILL its owner, reconnect; the old process was gone before the fresh app-server initialized. No provider inference, saved credentials, or operator gateway were used. The landed PR's exact-head [CI 33260972583](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/33260972583) is successful.

Named follow-up — **kernel process identity and terminal orphan custody**: the landed macOS inspector still uses second-resolution `ps lstart`, and failed orphan containment can resume the stale root. The remaining hardening work is to retain a stronger kernel identity for roots and descendants through every signal, and keep orphan containment terminal when concurrent recovery attempts overlap. This branch preserves an implementation and failing-before/passing-after same-second PID-reuse regressions, safe-unwind cases, and a kernel-disappearance-before-ps race regression. That extra hardening is not merged by #132610 or this PR. It should be integrated into the landed canonical registration/inspection flow, preserving its Alpine procfs support, early lifecycle observers, and acquisition deadline handling; do not bring over a second registry.

Evidence retained here: 34 focused macOS tests and 339 clean Linux tests passed on this branch. Its native Codex 0.150.1 proof passed. No claim is made that this duplicate branch's pending/conflicted CI or unfinished build passed. The redundant Testbox run was stopped.

Pre-merge proof for `543ebb8bc68a0da98da5bd9a406af4eedf8b4d76`:

The reported 120-second hang is reproduced on macOS Node 24.20.0. It occurs at HTTP listen, before client construction or WebSocket upgrade: the runner's nested temp path makes the socket pathname 112 bytes, so bind emits `EINVAL`; ws's earlier error-forwarding listener prevents the later rejection handler from running. The fixed fixture uses a short macOS temp path and binds before attaching ws. A deliberately invalid-path probe now rejects immediately. Production transport and timeouts are unchanged.

`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/transport-websocket.test.ts` passes all 8 tests, including the Unix JSON-RPC flow and all TCP sibling cases. Direct pinned ws 8.21.3 probes pass upgrade, message exchange, and shutdown on Node 24.20.0 and 26.7.0. Codex autoreview is clean; production LOC +0/-0, tests +8/-5. No additional test was added because the existing real-socket regression is the failure and now passes unchanged assertions.

[Exact-head CI run 33257687490](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/33257687490) is green, including changed-plugin tests, test/production types, lint/boundaries, and `openclaw/ci-gate`. payload.author: steipete
payload.body:
Addressed the lstart-granularity P1 in [ad232a32f7c](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/ad232a32f7cc3ccd0fc993d794e4ec4396111964): registration records the exact process command line, and the kill path rechecks it before the final PID/start-time check. A different command removes the stale row without signaling; an absent or failed read retains the row and never kills. The forbidden-replacement regression, “never kills a same-second replacement process running a different command,” fails without this gate. Registry suites pass 41/41; lint, format, both typechecks, and fresh Codex autoreview are clean.

The accepted tradeoff is command equality plus PID/start time, not a unique process-generation ID: Linux /proc starttime ticks were considered and rejected as a cross-platform solution because macOS has no /proc equivalent reachable from Node. A remaining kill collision would require the same second, PID, and identical command. The own-row residual—gateway PID reuse within the same one-second lstart bucket—is accepted: both owners are gateways, so command equality adds no distinction, and the consequence is a skipped cleanup pass rather than a wrong kill.

payload.author: steipete
payload.body:
Closing as superseded by #132610 (10ee252b56d), which landed the same follow-up 3 from #132413 while this PR was in review, with same-or-better coverage on every axis:

- Spawn-time registration in the same plugin keyed store namespace (`app-server-processes`), committed **blocking pre-initialize** with a verified `ppid` binding, and the child is killed if registration fails (`transport-process-registration.ts:56-95`) — strictly stronger than this PR's fire-and-forget registration, which accepted a small unregistered spawn window.
- Reap runs **before every spawn** with a fail-closed spawn refusal on cleanup failure (`transport-process-registration.ts:33-55`) — stronger than this PR's memoized once-per-boot pass.
- Zombie owners are treated as dead (`transport-process-registration.ts:46`), and the observer-in-snapshot guard exists (`:40`), matching the first two ClawSweeper findings here; pid-reuse of the owner is handled structurally (UUID row keys + pure identity comparison, no numeric own-pid exemption).
- The kill path SIGSTOP-quiesces the whole descendant tree via the existing containment machinery, revalidates identity, and verifies the process is actually gone before reporting success (`transport-process-containment.ts:27-67`) — stronger than this PR's single final per-pid confirmation.
- Additionally covers Linux via /proc without procps, the `codex exec-server` sibling child (`node-exec-server.runtime.ts`), ships docs, and proves behavior with a real-binary orphan e2e (`transport-orphan.test.ts`).

Two deltas from this PR's review rounds do not exist on main and are filed as follow-up work rather than blocking this close:

1. The lstart 1-second granularity collision gate (third ClawSweeper finding here): pid+pgid+lstart can theoretically match a same-second pid-reuse replacement; this PR added a `ps -o command=` byte-equality gate on the kill path with a forbidden-replacement regression (ad232a32f7c). The same class exists in the landed version and the ready-made regression can be ported.
2. Boot-time reaping: the landed version reaps at next spawn, not at gateway startup, so a wedged-drain orphan persists until codex is next used.

Evidence that would reopen: a demonstration that the landed reap-before-spawn path misses an orphan class this PR's boot-time service caught that upstream codex 0.150.1's stdin-EOF drain (rust-v0.150.1 `app-server/src/lib.rs:1038`, 30s+10s+10s bounded drains) does not self-resolve.

Thanks @clawsweeper for three genuine identity findings (zombie owners, owner pid reuse, lstart granularity) — two are structurally covered by the landed version and the third is now tracked follow-up work.

## Land-ready verification

Verified candidate: `8f19112e90f7872f042353afbead024e085d88f4`. This completes the isolated Gateway/Control UI evidence requested in the latest ClawSweeper review. Exact-head [CI run 33255432806](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/33255432806) is green, including `openclaw/ci-gate` and the SQLite session-lifecycle check. The PR head has not changed since this proof.

### Observed behavior

The original real SessionManager/SQLite repro returned one visible message after reset, then three after compaction, including two pre-reset messages. With this repair it remains one, with zero pre-reset messages; model context excludes those messages before and after the repair. Four message-window cases failed before the first owner repair, and four marker cases failed before the second owner repair.

The attached recording uses a real built Gateway, its bundled Control UI, real session lifecycle/compaction and real SQLite. Only the model HTTP endpoint is the repository's existing synthetic OpenAI-compatible fixture. All writes were performed through the normal composer: three old exchanges, `/compact`, `/clear` (same-session reset), three fresh exchanges, `/compact`, then reload and history traversal. Manual client compaction used the supported `default` mode; this is not a live external-provider or safeguard-quality-audit claim.

All 117 target-flow assertions passed: the same session identity survived reset; old message IDs and the old compaction marker stayed absent after subsequent compaction, reload, pagination and old-ID lookup; all six fresh dialogue rows remained; the new reset/compaction markers were correctly placed. The post-reset provider requests also contained no old conversation sentinels. Screenshots and sampled video frames were inspected. The media contains only synthetic conversation data and generic UI, and its upload was explicitly approved.

The video is **after-fix live evidence**. Before-fix evidence is the failing real-SQLite regression/API reproduction, not the pre-reset stage of this recording.

### Provenance

The boundary-selection behavior originated in [the cursor-preserving reset change](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/112988), authored and merged by @steipete on July 23, 2026; the marker projection carried it into [the database-backed boundary-divider change](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/122222), also authored and merged by @steipete on August 11. The original reset change intentionally retained broad latest-boundary shadowing. This explicitly requested repair applies the current reset-only history contract while preserving latest-reset-or-compaction model context; it is not an unexamined deletion of that earlier policy. The current repair is authored by @steipete.

### Ownership and compatibility

Best-fix verdict: the canonical owner repair, not a downstream mitigation. History selects the latest reset in both cold lookup and cache refresh; model-context accounting still selects the latest reset or compaction. The shared event-history projection drops earlier boundaries and rebases marker placement through the same logical message window. Consumer guards and treating compaction as a history reset were rejected because they either duplicate policy or discard valid current-window history.

The review's serialized-state detector is not a schema/migration change here: the production diff changes read-only selection/projection logic, with no table, column, index, schema version, persisted representation, writer, retention, concurrency or raw transcript mutation. The [read-only-query checkpoint exception](https://docs.openclaw.ai/reference/database-schemas#review-checkpoint-for-material-changes) applies. Upstream context-eligibility and display-position changes are preserved, not added by this PR.

payload.author: HuzaifaChaudary
payload.body:
ran it through the real wizard step rather than a mocked one, and it turned up a second thing worth having.

no vitest, no module mocks. real bundled plugin registry, real metadata snapshot, real activation resolver, real config shape. the only substitution is the human at the keyboard, and `WizardPrompter` is an injected dependency of `setupPluginConfig` by design, so supplying one is using the entrypoint rather than bypassing it. the prompter records what the multiselect is offered and then skips.

**before**

```
xai explicitly disabled in config
  plugins offered : __skip__, github-copilot, google, huggingface, minimax, moonshot, ollama,
                    opencode, xai, acpx, amazon-bedrock, amazon-bedrock-mantle, anthropic,
                    device-pair, geolocation, google-meet, linux-node, teams-meetings, zoom-meetings
  xai offered     : true

disabled config offers xai : true   (want false)
```

**after**

```
xai explicitly disabled in config
  plugins offered : __skip__, github-copilot, google, huggingface, minimax, moonshot, ollama,
                    opencode, acpx, amazon-bedrock, amazon-bedrock-mantle, anthropic,
                    device-pair, geolocation, google-meet, linux-node, teams-meetings,
                    memory-core, zoom-meetings
  xai offered     : false

no entry for xai, manifest default applies
  xai offered     : true
```

so `xai` is gone when config disables it, and still offered when nothing disables it, which is the manifest default doing its job.

**the part i did not expect.** diffing the two lists:

```
wrongly offered before, now gone : ['xai']
missed before, now offered       : ['memory-core']
```

`memory-core` was missing from the old list entirely. that is the other half of the issue, a plugin activated through canonical slot policy rather than an explicit entry, which `enabledByDefault || entry.enabled === true` had no way to see. the wizard was not asking about a plugin that runs. i had only written a test for the first direction, so this is worth having on the record.

the script is nine lines of prompter plus two calls, so rather than carry it in the branch:

```ts
import { setupPluginConfig } from "./src/wizard/setup.plugin-config.js";
const offered: string[] = [];
const prompter = { /* ...noop, multiselect records opts.options and returns ["__skip__"] */ };
await setupPluginConfig({ config: { plugins: { entries: { xai: { enabled: false } } } }, prompter });
console.log(offered.includes("xai"));
```

run with `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs <file>.mts` on node 24.20.0 and pnpm 12.0.0.

happy to add the `memory-core` direction as a second regression test if you want it pinned, though it depends on which plugins are bundled so it may be better asserted against a synthetic slot-activated manifest than against `memory-core` by name. say which you would prefer.

Thanks @yetval!

**Proof:** A real background command was left running for the maintenance grace period. On main, standalone `tasks maintenance --apply` changed its row from `running` to `lost`. On the merged repair, maintenance reconciled zero tasks, kept the row `running`, observed the command's unique completion output, and stored `succeeded` with `Command completed`.

- **Fix:** Non-authoritative maintenance now retains process-local CLI rows, while Gateway maintenance still reclaims confirmed orphaned work.

**Maintainer decision:** retain configured-reference ownership and the intentional no-fallback outcome. An explicitly configured structured env ref with an absent/empty selected value is `blocked`, not permission to borrow an auth-profile credential. This follows the explicitly requested no-credential-fallback invariant. Genuinely absent credential input retains ordinary fallback; operators can supply the selected env value or remove the explicit ref if they intend to use existing profile selection. This decision and the green exact-head checks satisfy the latest ClawSweeper rank-up moves. Its review found no code/security defect.

The remaining Feishu CI failure was a stale discovery fixture treating a selected default as a forbidden mismatch. payload.body:
the regression-test gap you named is real and worth fixing on its own, so i did that rather than only answer the proof line.

> The new tests call the new predicate and applyConfigSnapshot directly; neither invokes saveConfigDraft nor crosses ConfigStore.save, so they cannot detect a later miswiring of the actual save completion.

correct. the new test goes through the real completion. it installs a `saveRemote` override that blocks, starts `saveConfigDraft()`, waits until the write is actually in flight, edits a still-enabled field, then releases the write:

```swift
let gate = SaveGate()
await ConfigStore._testSetOverrides(.init(
    isRemoteMode: { true },
    saveRemote: { _ in await gate.wait() }))

let saving = Task { await store.saveConfigDraft() }
await gate.waitUntilEntered()
store.updateConfigValue(path: [.key("channels"), .key("discord"), .key("enabled")], value: true)
await gate.release()
await saving.value
```

the observable is that a raced save leaves no load behind it. `loadConfig(force: false)` returns before it asks the gateway for anything, so nothing is fetched and nothing is republished.

putting the forced call back, everything else identical:

```
✘ "a real save that is raced by an edit does not reload over it"
    Expectation failed: (store.configStatus →
      "gateway connect: connect to gateway @ ws://127.0.0.1:18789: Could not connect to the server.")
      == nil
```

that error is the reload the fix removes, recorded by the save completion itself. on this branch the same test passes and `configStatus` stays nil. 14/14 in `ChannelsSettingsSmokeTests`.

two things worth stating plainly rather than leaving you to infer them.

**this is terminal output, not a settings-flow recording.** you listed a trace or runtime log as acceptable, so i took that route. i cannot run `screencapture` on this machine, it returns `could not create image from display`, so a recording of the real Settings pane is not something i can produce here. if the flow recording is required rather than one of the alternatives, say so and i will ask the machine owner to capture it.

**the test asserts the reload is skipped, not that a fetched snapshot fails to overwrite.** `loadConfig` reads through `GatewayConnection.shared.requestDecoded`, which has no test seam, so i cannot stand up a gateway that returns the older saved values and show the overwrite landing. skipping the reload is the mechanism the fix relies on, and it is what the test pins. i would rather name that boundary than let the evidence read as broader than it is.

if a real settings flow capture is required for this one, it needs someone with a running gateway rather than another artefact from me. #132565 was different because the talk overlay owns its own panel and needs nothing external, which is why the screenshots worked there and cannot work here.

`TalkOverlayRenderProbe` (`2d09b0d8`) drives the real `TalkOverlayController` through present, dismiss, present, waits past the 160 ms fade, then renders the real overlay view and composites it at the panel's own `alphaValue`, drawing nothing when the panel is ordered out. that composite is what reaches the screen.

| | after present | after the interrupted dismissal |
|---|---|---|
| base | ![base presented](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/HuzaifaChaudary/openclaw/evidence/talk-overlay-127645/talk-overlay-127645/before-1-presented.png) | ![base gone](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/HuzaifaChaudary/openclaw/evidence/talk-overlay-127645/talk-overlay-127645/before-2-after-interrupted-dismissal.png) |

the second base frame is empty. Talk is still enabled, and the panel is transparent and ordered out:

```

base    PROBE 2-after-interrupted-dismissal:  visible=false alpha=0.0
branch  PROBE 1-presented:                    visible=true  alpha=1.0
branch  PROBE 2-after-interrupted-dismissal:  visible=true  alpha=1.0
```

payload.author: obviyus
payload.body:
Thanks to the Discord reporter!

| Item | Details |
| --- | --- |
| **Bug** | Guided llama.cpp setup downloaded the default Q8 embedding model even when local memory selected a configured Q4 model. The first memory search then downloaded Q4 and rewrote the preset. |
| **Fix** | Setup now uses the same embedding-model resolver as runtime, reads effective enabled-agent settings, ignores disabled and non-local agents, and stops before mutation when enabled local agents disagree. |
| **Example** | **Before:** Q4 config caused a Q8 download followed by a Q4 download. **After:** setup downloads only Q4, keeps `models: []`, and preserves the selected chat model. |
| **Proof** | In an isolated 8 GiB Ubuntu virtual machine, current main reproduced the Q8-then-Q4 behavior. The merged head installed only the verified 277,852,192-byte Q4 model, passed `/health`, returned two different 768-value embeddings, completed hybrid memory search, passed 136 plugin tests and exact-head CI, and passed ClawSweeper with no findings or security concerns. Conflicting enabled agents stopped before consent or mutation, while disabled and non-local stale paths were ignored. |

payload.author: psewar
payload.body:
Heads-up for maintainers: ClawSweeper appears to be stuck in a restart loop on this PR, and it is burning worker time on your side.

**Symptom:** since the PR was opened at 09:59Z (now ~18:49Z), the author has received ~80 notification emails, each containing:

> ClawSweeper status: review started. I am starting a fresh review of this pull request … This is item 1/1 in the current shard. Shard 0/1.

**What the API shows:** the PR currently has exactly one ClawSweeper comment — the original `clawsweeper-pr-ack:opened` from 09:59:32Z, with `updated_at` identical to `created_at`. The "review started" comment is not present. So it is being created (sending a mail) and deleted again, roughly every seven minutes for nine hours. Deleted comments leave no trace in the comment list or the timeline, which is why the PR looks quiet from outside.

**Not repo-wide:** other open PRs get completed reviews (e.g. #132770, #132769 show "Codex review: …"), so the worker is healthy elsewhere. This PR seems to be a specific trigger.

**Possibly related:** `check-lint` on run 33246753409 did not fail on a lint error — the job was killed mid-run:

```
[oxlint:extensions] still running after 122s
##[error]The runner has received a shutdown signal.
##[error]The operation was canceled.
```

`openclaw/ci-gate` then failed in 3s as a mirror of that status. If the review worker waits for check results that never arrived, that would fit the restart pattern. A re-run of that job may be all it needs — I cannot trigger one from a fork.

I am happy to close and reopen, convert to draft, or rebase if any of that helps you stop the loop; just say which. Flagging it rather than sitting on it, since the retries cost you compute.

Confirmed the pinned upstream source directly: Gemini v0.57.0 calls native compression before requests (`client.ts:643`), installs the compressed history with the same recording service (`client.ts:1114–1164`), and synchronizes that history into its resumable record (`geminiChat.ts:368–416`). The linked real Gemini Docker flow passed first/resume turns and admitted-agent MCP create/identity/cleanup; exact-head CI33245670749 is green.

The manual-compaction implication is intentional and documented. The prior generic path did not invoke Gemini's native compactor; it used a separate OpenClaw summarizer requiring separate API authentication and could replace the native resume binding. Keeping that path would preserve the same ownership defect this repair addresses. Gemini has no declared manual compaction adapter, so the existing capability guard now reports that limitation explicitly. This change does not claim a new native manual command, and adds no credential fallback or config option. The automatic path retains actual Claude/generic/native-harness sibling coverage.

This records the maintainer decision under the authorized repair sweep and answers the review's source/live-proof rank-up request. No public SDK capability is removed; the existing owner declaration is corrected.

payload.author: wangmiao0668000666
payload.body:
Closing this PR — the exact-head CI failure led me to evidence that falsifies this PR's premise.

**What the CI failure showed:** `checks-node-compact-small-10` fails in `src/gateway/server.chat.acp-completion.test.ts` (`completes 'persistence errors' once with truthful transcript ownership`). That gateway test pins the exact behavior this PR tries to change: an operational transcript-persistence failure produces `status: "error"` and a transcript containing only the user row.

**Why that changes the picture:** I claimed in this PR (and in #132516) that the removal of `try/catch + logVerbose` in #132040 was an incidental, untested side effect of the session-fence work. That is wrong: `server.chat.acp-completion.test.ts` (439 lines) was added in the *same* commit `1c40abdb63b`, whose message states the intent — "give ACP replies one completion owner" with truthful transcript ownership: the run's terminal state must reflect whether the transcript was actually persisted. The fail-visible behavior for operational persistence failures is deliberate maintainer design with dedicated test coverage, not an accidental regression.

My due diligence missed this because my pre/post-fix runs only covered the `src/auto-reply` lane; the pinning test lives in the gateway lane. Apologies for the noise — closing this PR and the issue.

Addressed the deadline review on head 178644bf873d33e61d90b2d46781d93665a0c11c. The reported early-expiry case does not reproduce: the reply caller passes the same operation age that it compares. At minute 20 with an absolute deadline at minute 30, the threshold is `20 + (30 - 20) = 30` minutes, so `20 > 30` is false. A tool starting at minute 10 does not change that calculation. Diagnostic and admission callers also use matching ages.

The helper parameter is now named `evidenceAgeMs`, with a short comment preserving the matching-clock contract. An additional regression case delays the first tool by 10 minutes, verifies freshness at minute 20 plus 1 ms, sends later progress, and verifies freshness exactly at minute 30 followed by expiry at minute 30 plus 1 ms. All six worker owner tests pass; scoped lint, formatting, and fresh Codex autoreview pass. This clarifies and protects existing behavior; it is not a runtime deadline change.

The separate provisioning-cancellation limitation is tracked in #132514. Current-head CI and the real cloud parent/child validation are still being completed before landing.

payload.author: wangmiao0668000666
payload.body:
Closing this PR — while building the requested real-boundary proof I obtained evidence that the reported defect is not observable with the production ledger, so the premise fails.

**Probe (real components, not mocks):** real `AcpTranslatorSessionUpdates` + real `createSqliteAcpEventLedger` (the exact production wiring from `src/acp/server.ts:255`) writing to a real SQLite state DB, with `connection.sessionUpdate` rejecting 50ms after each call (mimicking a dead-client EPIPE arriving on a later macrotask). Three recorded `agent_message_chunk` emits, then the DB was dumped.

**Result — identical pre-fix and post-fix:**

```text
$ node --import scripts/tsx.mjs emit-ledger-probe.mts <state-dir>
[emit 1] rejected: Error: client gone (EPIPE)
[emit 2] rejected: Error: client gone (EPIPE)
[emit 3] rejected: Error: client gone (EPIPE)
[ledger] 3 rows
[ledger] seq=1 text=chunk-1
[ledger] seq=2 text=chunk-2
[ledger] seq=3 text=chunk-3
```

Current `main` (without this PR) produces the same 3 rows as the patched code.

**Why:** `enqueueLedgerMutation` schedules the write onto the session's mutation chain at `emit()` call time, and the SQLite ledger body is fully synchronous (`runSqliteImmediateTransactionSync` via `runOpenClawStateWriteTransaction`). The mutation therefore runs at the next microtask flush — always before any later macrotask such as the delivery-rejection event, stdin EOF, or process exit. Skipping `await recording` after a rejected delivery loses the *ordering guarantee* on paper, but with the production ledger the row has already landed before the rejection even arrives. My regression test used a 20ms-deferred mock ledger; that timing cannot occur with the real SQLite (or in-memory) ledger, so the test pinned a scenario the production boundary never produces. Corroborating readings: gateway events are dispatched independently (`server.ts:162`, `void ...catch(log)`), so one chunk's delivery failure does not abort later chunks' recording; shutdown revokes ledger access before transport teardown by design (`server.ts:202-206`).

The remaining value of this change would be defending against a hypothetical future async ledger implementation — speculative resilience the repo's own doctrine treats as a defect. Closing this PR and the issue. Sorry for the noise; the probe script and reasoning above are the evidence.

Codex review: found issues before merge. _Reviewed August 29, 2026, 4:02 PM ET / 20:02 UTC._ # ClawSweeper review ## What this changes The branch renders credential-bound usage, billing, errors, and refresh state in Models-page account rows while retaining separate provider and session metrics. ## Merge readiness ⚠️ **Ready for maintainer review - 3 items remain** Keep open: the new UI can hide provider-wide Admin usage whenever account usage is also present and the supplemental usage request has not succeeded. **Priority:** P2 **Reviewed head:** `476185970a593b084629184c8aa1dd599d468f25` ## Review scores | Measure | Result | What it means | |---|---|---| | **Overall readiness** | 🦐 gold shrimp **(3/6)** | The implementation has focused tests and a clear UI goal, but a source-proven mixed provider/profile usage regression blocks merge. | | **Proof confidence** | 🌊 off-meta tidepool | Not applicable: Not applicable to the external-contributor proof gate because this is a member-authored PR; its supplied body reports exact-head localhost and screenshot evidence, but the reviewer could not retrieve hosted artifacts through DNS. | | **Patch quality** | 🦐 gold shrimp **(3/6)** | 1 actionable review finding remain. | ## Verification | Check | Result | Evidence | |---|---|---| | **Real behavior** | Not applicable | Not applicable: Not applicable to the external-contributor proof gate because this is a member-authored PR; its supplied body reports exact-head localhost and screenshot evidence, but the reviewer could not retrieve hosted artifacts through DNS. | | **Evidence reviewed** | 5 items | Current main behavior: Current main renders a single provider-wide usage section after the credential summary and has no account-row renderer, so the requested per-account presentation is not already implemented.
Provider-wide and profile usage coexist: The stacked Gateway producer separately obtains provider-wide usage for Admin credentials and exact-profile usage, then prefers the provider-wide value on the provider row.
Introduced suppression loses that distinction: The new card flag is set only when the separate usage.status payload is present, while the new rendering condition hides provider usage when profile usage exists and that flag is absent. | | **Findings** | 1 actionable finding | [P2] Preserve provider-wide usage when profile usage is populated | | **Security** | None | None. | ## How this fits together Gateway status supplies account and provider usage to the Control UI. The Models page combines those signals into provider cards, then presents account-specific capacity alongside provider-wide history. ```mermaid flowchart LR A[Saved credentials] --> B[Gateway usage status] B --> C[Models page data] C --> D[Provider card] D --> E[Account usage rows] D --> F[Provider-wide metrics] E --> G[Models page] F --> G ``` ## Before merge - [ ] **Preserve provider-wide usage when profile usage is populated (P2)** - This condition hides `card.usage` whenever any profile has usage unless the separate `usage.status` load has marked it independent. The Gateway can already attach Admin-derived provider-wide history and exact OAuth usage in the same `models.authStatus` response, so the provider-wide history disappears until that supplemental request succeeds—and remains absent if it fails. Carry the usage origin through the card data instead of using supplemental completion as the discriminator; the current test only injects `usageIndependent` directly. - [ ] **Resolve merge risk (P1)** - An operator with both Admin provider history and OAuth account quotas can lose the provider-wide history from the card while the separate usage.status request is pending or fails. - [ ] **Complete next step (P2)** - The repair spans the open Gateway parent and this stacked UI consumer, so its producer-side provenance contract should be reviewed together before updating the stack. ## Findings - [P2] Preserve provider-wide usag

See [Decision needed](#decision-needed). ## Review scores | Measure | Result | What it means | |---|---|---| | **Overall readiness** | 🦐 gold shrimp **(3/6)** | The patch has coherent source and focused test coverage, but its new provider API commitment and external response-field contract need maintainer confirmation. | | **Proof confidence** | 🌊 off-meta tidepool | Not applicable: The author is a repository MEMBER, so the external-contributor proof gate does not apply; the body reports a redacted four-account local run, while the reviewed source and tests cover the profile-binding and cache boundaries. | | **Patch quality** | 🦐 gold shrimp **(3/6)** | No actionable review findings were identified. | ## Verification | Check | Result | Evidence | |---|---|---| | **Real behavior** | Not applicable | Not applicable: The author is a repository MEMBER, so the external-contributor proof gate does not apply; the body reports a redacted four-account local run, while the reviewed source and tests cover the profile-binding and cache boundaries. | | **Evidence reviewed** | 7 items | Exact-profile owner boundary: The resolver confines plugin helpers and generic OAuth resolution to the requested profile and disables profile fallback before returning the credential.
Gateway caller and cache consumer: The gateway creates usage targets only for saved OAuth/token profiles, excludes externally managed CLI profiles, and passes each target to the bounded profile cache.
Plugin contract documentation: The added documentation defines authProfileId as an exact saved-account request and prohibits credential substitution; the matching type carries that optional context to providers. | | **Findings** | None | None. | | **Security** | None | None. | ## How this fits together The gateway reports configured provider accounts to control-plane clients and enriches them with provider usage data. This change binds each enrichment request to one saved credential, then returns the resulting usage state on that account. ```mermaid flowchart LR A[Saved provider accounts] --> B[Gateway auth status] B --> C[Exact-profile auth resolver] C --> D[Provider usage hook] D --> E[Bounded usage cache] E --> F[Account usage response] ``` ## Decision needed | Question | Recommendation | |---|---| | Should OpenClaw support the new durable per-profile usage contract for provider plugins and models.authStatus clients? | **Accept the profile-bound contract:** Adopt the documented exact-profile usage semantics after the API owner confirms the external-plugin and client compatibility commitment. | Why: This is an additive provider/plugin API and gateway response feature, not a mechanical bug repair; compatibility scope and support commitment require maintainer intent. ## Before merge - [ ] **Resolve merge risk (P1)** - The additive provider-plugin usage context and gateway response fields need owner acceptance as a durable compatibility contract for external plugins and clients. - [ ] **Resolve merge risk (P1)** - The newly parsed ChatGPT usage response fields have fixture coverage and reported local-account evidence, but no independently readable upstream response contract was available in this review. - [ ] **Complete next step (P2)**

The new roster turns profile IDs into visible account identities for read-only viewers, despite the Gateway intentionally withholding account email and display metadata from that scope. **Priority:** P1 **Reviewed head:** `b3240b545ce2198fa394c589d53927075712c03e` **Owner decision:** Required. See [Decision needed](#decision-needed). ## Review scores | Measure | Result | What it means | |---|---|---| | **Overall readiness** | 🦐 gold shrimp **(3/6)** | The roster implementation has meaningful validation evidence, but the unresolved P1 read-only identity disclosure blocks merge readiness. | | **Proof confidence** | 🌊 off-meta tidepool | Not applicable: This MEMBER-authored PR is exempt from the external-contributor proof gate; its supplied roster screenshot and local-Gateway keyboard trace support the intended UI behavior but do not resolve the read-only privacy regression. | | **Patch quality** | 🦐 gold shrimp **(3/6)** | Security review found an item that needs attention. | ## Verification | Check | Result | Evidence | |---|---|---| | **Real behavior** | Not applicable | Not applicable: This MEMBER-authored PR is exempt from the external-contributor proof gate; its supplied roster screenshot and local-Gateway keyboard trace support the intended UI behavior but do not resolve the read-only privacy regression. | | **Evidence reviewed** | 5 items | Introduced identity rendering: The PR adds the roster and makes profileId the identity fallback, then renders it as visible text, title, aria-label input, and DOM data attributes.
Gateway read-only privacy contract: models.authStatus always includes profileId, but only includes profile email and displayName when the connecting client has operator.admin.
Existing privacy regression coverage: The Gateway suite explicitly verifies that operator.read omits profile email and displayName, establishing that account identity is intentionally restricted even though profileId remains in the payload. | | **Findings** | 1 actionable finding | [P1] Prevent account-ID exposure to read-only viewers | | **Security** | Needs attention | Read-only roster exposes profile identity: The Gateway withholds account email and display metadata for operator.read, but the new client-side fallback displays and serializes the raw profile ID, which may contain an email-form account identifier. | ## How this fits together The Models page receives provider account status from the Gateway and displays it to Control UI users. The new roster renders each account and sends authorized reorder or logout actions back through the Gateway. ```mermaid flowchart LR A[Gateway account status] --> B[Models page data] B --> C[Provider account roster] C --> D{Viewer scope} D --> E[Read-only viewer] D --> F[Administrator] E --> G[Account identity display] F --> H[Reorder and logout actions] ``` ## Decision needed | Question | Recommendation | |---|---| | Should the detailed provider-account roster be administrator-only, or should the Gateway define a non-identifying read-only representation for it? | **Restrict the roster to administrators:** Render the detailed roster only for operator-admin clients and preserve the existing read-only provider summary. | Why: The existing Gateway contract hides account metadata from operator.read, but choosing whether read-only users retain a redacted roster is a product and security-boundary decision. ## Before merge - [ ] **Prevent account-ID exposure to read-only viewers (P1)** - The Gateway deliberately omits profile `email`

See [Decision needed](#decision-needed). ## Review scores | Measure | Result | What it means | |---|---|---| | **Overall readiness** | 🐚 platinum hermit **(4/6)** | The patch has coherent owner-boundary integration and focused coverage; remaining readiness depends on accepting the new public routing contract. | | **Proof confidence** | 🦞 diamond lobster **(5/6)** | Not applicable: This member-authored PR is exempt from the external-contributor proof gate; its supplied local-Gateway terminal trace nevertheless maps the new handler to reordered status/model-runtime publication and observed persistence. | | **Patch quality** | 🐚 platinum hermit **(4/6)** | No actionable review findings were identified. | ## Verification | Check | Result | Evidence | |---|---|---| | **Real behavior** | Not applicable | Not applicable: This member-authored PR is exempt from the external-contributor proof gate; its supplied local-Gateway terminal trace nevertheless maps the new handler to reordered status/model-runtime publication and observed persistence. | | **Evidence reviewed** | 5 items | Write-path and publication ordering: The introduced handler validates provider-owned profiles, writes through the existing auth-profile owner, refreshes affected prepared runtimes, and only then acknowledges success.
Existing selection owner: Model selection already resolves stored order before configured/default ordering, so the new operation changes a real provider-routing preference rather than introducing a parallel store.
Authorization and protocol registration: The new method is appended to the Gateway compatibility tail and classified as an operator-admin control-plane write. | | **Findings** | None | None. | | **Security** | None | None. | ## How this fits together The Gateway exposes auth-profile status to operator clients and reads the same profile store used by model selection. Codex review: needs maintainer review before merge. _Reviewed August 29, 2026, 3:32 AM ET / 07:32 UTC._ # ClawSweeper review ## What this changes The PR lets owned Node worker processes settle after IPC disconnection, exit, and closure of all non-stdin pipes when Node omits the child close event. ## Merge readiness ⚠️ **Ready for maintainer review - 2 items remain** No new actionable defect was found. The PR remains necessary because current main only has the Windows exit-and-drain settlement path; this adds the missing owned POSIX worker boundary, and its protected maintainer label requires normal maintainer review. **Priority:** P2 **Reviewed head:** `81fda09b70c24ea2905998e543766f2adcd65ac6` ## Review scores | Measure | Result | What it means | |---|---|---| | **Overall readiness** | 🐚 platinum hermit **(4/6)** | A focused lifecycle repair with strong ordering and sibling coverage; exact-head checks remain the appropriate final merge gate. | | **Proof confidence** | 🌊 off-meta tidepool | Not applicable: Not applicable to this maintainer-authored PR. The supplied body nevertheless describes a real managed-IPC entry run and a real supervisor scenario tied to the changed child adapter; that is supportive evidence, not an external-contributor proof gate. | | **Patch quality** | 🐚 platinum hermit **(4/6)** | No actionable review findings were identified. | ## Verification | Check | Result | Evidence | |---|---|---| | **Real behavior** | Not applicable | Not applicable: Not applicable to this maintainer-authored PR. The supplied body nevertheless describes a real managed-IPC entry run and a real supervisor scenario tied to the changed child adapter; that is supportive evidence, not an external-contributor proof gate. | | **Evidence reviewed** | 7 items | Current-main gap: Current main restricts exit-and-drained-pipe settlement to Windows, so it does not implement the owned POSIX worker behavior requested here.
Introduced completion boundary: The introduced adapter logic requires an owned worker's IPC disconnect, process exit, drained stdout/stderr, and closure of every additional non-stdin descriptor before resolving wait; ordinary POSIX children remain on child close.
Production caller and downstream owner: The local worker transport is the only changed-path caller and creates the adapter with ownedWorker plus private IPC; its observer then persists the outcome and capacity publishes the resulting free slot. | | **Findings** | None | None. | | **Security** | None | None. | ## How this fits together The Node worker supervisor starts isolated worker processes and releases their capacity slot after the child adapter observes physical completion. The adapter feeds the worker observer, which persists a terminal receipt and publishes the released capacity. ```mermaid flowchart LR A[Node worker process] --> B[IPC disconnect] A --> C[Exit and pipe closure] B --> D[Child process adapter] C --> D D --> E[Worker output observer] E --> F[Terminal receipt] F --> G[Capacity released] ``` ## Before merge - [ ] **Resolve merge risk (P1)** - This changes the physical-completion boundary that releases worker capacity; an unrepresented Node event ordering could still cause premature release or retention, although the IPC/exit/pipe permutations, secret descriptor, ordinary-child, and Windows tests constrain it. - [ ] **Resolve merge risk (P1)** - The local checkout has no inspectable Node child-process source/types and network resolution failed, so direct upstream confirmation of the Node event-order contract was infeasible; the source review therefore relies on the public-event implementation and focused regression coverage.

Maintainer decision: adopt retries that require a recognized transient signature. An opaque lane timeout should fail after retaining diagnostics, preserving the remaining job budget for other selected work. Recognized rate-limit, capacity and network failures remain eligible for retry. An unclassified transient can now fail after one attempt; that is the accepted tradeoff within this release-verification speedup. No deadline, lane, scenario, assertion or candidate-identity check is weakened.

Personal owner review caught the initial signal-order gap: EXIT cleanup inherited the harness function's output redirection and could print back into its own input log. Corrected head `3c5876b4288022ed3ebad45acfd1a3ae7072daee` reserves the original output descriptor. The actual harness regression failed on four signal cases before correction, then passed with bounded output once, preserved stdin/container cleanup and statuses 129/130/143. My independent original reproduction also now returns 143 with one visible tail and no remaining log.

The full scheduler/observability proof passes 20 tests, logging/container-FD siblings pass 15, and Bash 3 observability passes 11. Exact-head CI and native preparation passed without changing or pushing the reviewed head. Current main has no overlapping owner changes. Tooling grows by nine net lines for the two cleanup owners and reserved descriptor; product runtime is unchanged.

I read the latest exact-head ClawSweeper review; this records its requested retry-policy acceptance, and its CI condition is satisfied. The underlying live plugin stall remains unknown. After landing, the prepared targeted OpenAI package replay will use tooling containing this merge to retain diagnostics; no full-release success is claimed here.

The runtime growth binds captured policy to its catalog owner and selected route, keeps internal dispatch on its host context, and preserves lazy metadata without a new config or fallback path.

CI coordination from the compaction repair: the four current-version database-fixture failures are fixed in this head's run, so #132564 is waiting for this repair rather than duplicating those hunks. The remaining failure in [run 33252249308 / job 99099913683](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/33252249308/job/99099913683) is `portal-stream-command.test.ts`'s IPv6 success case: expected `echo:hello`, received `HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request`.

I reproduced a fixture state producing that exact response with real sockets and the actual `invokeNodeWorkerPortalStream` implementation, without changing production code:

1. Bind the echo server to an ephemeral IPv6 loopback port.
2. Bind the synthetic HTTP/WebSocket Gateway to IPv4 loopback at the **same numeric port**; those separate-family binds are both valid.
3. Use the valid IPv4-first `localhost` ordering and invoke the normal portal command for the echo port.
4. Attach succeeds, but `hello` reaches the HTTP server and yields the observed 400 response. Reserving the Gateway's port across both families instead yields `echo:hello`; both runs close their owned sockets/listeners.

The current fixture allocates each server with port 0 on different address families, so it does not exclude this state. `autoSelectFamily` has no application-protocol identity check, nor should this test add one to production. The CI log does not record the two allocated ports, so I cannot retroactively prove that this particular run collided; this is a deterministic reproduction of a real fixture hazard matching its failure.

Please keep any repair fixture-owned: make the synthetic Gateway's allocation exclude the echo endpoint across address families (for example, a dual-stack reservation), retain the IPv6-only echo coverage and real transport, and keep the existing assertions. No production localhost policy change, retries, weakened assertion, or SQLite change is needed for the reproduced hazard. The earlier refusal-case port-order fix does not cover this success case. No portal source/test file has been edited, and I have not touched this PR's active checkout or branch.

**Audit growth on parked re-polls (P2 + merge risk)**: fixed. `ReefMessageFlow` now keeps the set of entry ids whose last outcome parked and skips the duplicate durable `read` observation on their re-polls — one read event per park lifecycle, normal observation resumes when the entry resolves. The flow-level regression asserts exactly one `read` audit entry across park → re-poll → approve → deliver.

**Relay ping/pong evidence (merge risk)**: direct relay source, not inference. The mailbox Durable Object in `openclaw/reef` (`workers/relay/src/mailbox.ts`, `webSocketMessage`) answers a literal `"ping"` string with `"pong"` and ignores other non-entry strings after a size check; that handler has existed since the relay's initial worker commit (`61630a3`, "Cloudflare Reef relay worker with per-handle inbox DOs"), which is an ancestor of the deployed relay (auto-deployed from reef `main` on push via `deploy-relay.yml`; last redeploy verified 2026-08-14). There has never been a deployed relay version without it. Post-land live verification on a production claw will additionally confirm keepalive behavior (no 1006 recurrence, no keepalive-timeout reconnects).

**Production LOC (merge risk)**: the growth is the named capability and security invariant, not padding: (1) the review store consulted before any guard call — closing an owner-review bypass — requires the `ReviewGate` lookup surface and the decided-redelivery paths; (2) parked-as-waiting-state semantics (typed error, cursor hold with completed-entry folding, poll re-attempt) is what removes the connection-teardown/retry-until-allow behavior; (3) the keepalive is a new capability the transport simply lacked. The shared `classifyApprovedDelivery` helper deduplicates the in-call and redelivery approval paths rather than growing them twice.

payload.author: steipete
payload.body:
Addressing the review findings on head c2e6d6cd660:

**[P1] Rearm settlement timeout when finalization hooks finish — refuted with an evidence-backed reproduction.** The claimed 30-minute wait is unreachable: every current-turn notification handler calls `turnWatches.touchActivity(...)` synchronously at entry (`attempt-notification-state.ts:116-120`, before awaiting its projector), which reschedules the terminal watch via `scheduleProgressWatches()`. After the hook-completed handler decrements the unsettled-hook count, any subsequently blocked handler has therefore already re-armed the watch, and fire-time re-evaluation selects the short settlement window. We built the exact ordered reproduction the review described — terminal received while a hook is pending, hook completes through the production decrement, the next handler blocks forever — and it settles within `TURN_TERMINAL_SETTLEMENT_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS + TURN_FINALIZE_DRAIN_ABORT_GRACE_MS` of fake time against the pre-existing code, not the 30-minute budget. That reproduction is now a committed regression ("settles blocked terminal delivery within the short window after a queued hook completes", `run-attempt.turn-watches.test.ts`). The unit test's `touchActivity` call mirrors this production entry touch rather than masking a gap. Residual corner: a non-turn-scoped handler (e.g. a config warning) blocking after hook settlement skips the entry touch; that ordering remains bounded by the 30-minute absolute budget, which is the deliberate backstop for counters the blocked tail can never settle.

**[P2] Exercise the Codex handler-stall path in the restart E2E — skip, stated.** The gateway e2e deliberately forces the built-in runtime: it proves the provider-agnostic startup-orphan invariant (SIGKILL with no drain marking → startup scan → recovery → a new send dispatches), which no existing test covered. The changed Codex router/watch/finalize surfaces are exercised end-to-end at the harness level by `run-attempt.test.ts` ("clears an active run with blocked terminal delivery after terminal timeout / user stop") and the new ordered-hook regression — those drive the real turn router, notification controller, watches, and finalization against a mock app-server, including `clearActiveEmbeddedRun`. A live Codex-runtime gateway e2e needs codex app-server auth that CI does not have; live-channel proof for this path stays a stronger-but-unavailable rank-up.

**Merge risk (net production growth)** — production is +61/−21 net +40 across the branch: the settlement constant + keeping the terminal watch alive (watch owner), the bounded drain joins (`turn-router.drain` racing route release; finalize racing abort with a 5s grace — finalize owns those joins, so the bound lives with the owner rather than as a new fallback layer), composed with #107721's abort-cleanup join. The invariant "an attempt reaches terminal outcome in bounded time" could not be expressed by deleting code on this surface.

Both review findings are addressed on head `dd40c96e121`:

The implementation decision was made by automation. No separate manual security-owner approval of that policy has been received, and this comment must not be used as evidence of such approval. **Native preparation and merge remain on hold.**

The candidate at `a91249fbec372701294b26a9689aba3e99645bf8` excludes a result from the GitHub upload only when it has one `inSource` suppression with absent status (the representation emitted by the pinned OpenGrep v1.27.1 producer) or explicit `accepted` status. Addressed the review — one fix applied, one product decision recorded, one skip stated.

**P2 "Derive dashboard availability from board state, not preferred face" — fixed by rewording.** The hovercard label now says **"Opens as dashboard"** (`sessionsView.opensAsDashboard`), which states exactly the recorded fact driving it: the session's persisted preferred face. **P1 semantic decision — maintainer-decided: preference fact, no owner projection.** The point of this PR is deleting the client-side `board.get` probe fleet whose only product was the old availability badge. Reintroducing an authoritative board-existence fact (server projection or probing) to feed a hovercard metadata row would rebuild the machinery this change removes, for a fact of marginal value: dashboard-face sessions communicate their nature by opening as the dashboard, and boards inside chat-face sessions remain fully discoverable in-session. Decision: the hovercard reports the recorded preference, honestly labeled.

**P1 real-capture rank-up — skip stated.** The attached before/after images are Playwright captures of the real Control UI in a real Chromium against the deterministic mocked Gateway (`pnpm dev:ui:mock -- --fixture workboard`), the repo-standard visual proof for Control UI presentation changes. No gateway behavior changed in this PR — the deleted controller, cache, and badges are all client-side — so an isolated live-Gateway video adds no coverage the mocked run lacks. The images were unretrievable to the reviewer due to a DNS failure in its environment; they render on the PR.

Tests updated for the new wording; focused suites and `check:changed` green on the new head.

payload.body:
Round-1 P1 addressed in `3fc14dd7b1c`.

**Fix (claim-first, nonblocking notice).** The `aborted` branch now mirrors `settleRecoveredPrompt`: `claimPendingPrompt(pending)` runs before the first `await`, the interruption chunk is emitted with `waitForDelivery: false`, and `finishPrompt(..., "cancelled", { claimed: true })` settles terminally. A stalled or rejected notice delivery can no longer strand the prompt. New regression test: `resolves as cancelled when the interruption notice delivery rejects` — fails on the review head (`1 failed | 21 passed`), passes post-fix (`22 passed`). Full ACP lane on the new head: 63 files / 571 tests green.

One scope note from that work: `finishPrompt`'s snapshot emit awaits client delivery on `main` for *every* stop reason, so a fully stalled client already holds settlement there — pre-existing, not widened by this PR. The regression suite covers the rejecting-client case rather than an infinitely stalled one.

**Real-behavior proof** (the missing gate): packaged `dist/` build of the exact head, isolated state dir; real Gateway + loopback mock OpenAI Responses provider + real `openclaw acp` bridge + ACP SDK client. The model emits `session_status` with schema-invalid arguments (real pre-execution validation failure — the actual `toolErrorSummary` producer), the follow-up request stalls, and a second operator connection aborts via `chat.abort` mid-run:

```text
acp: sessionUpdate tool_call_update status=failed — Validation failed for tool "session_status": changesSince: must be integer
gateway: chat.abort { sessionKey } → { ok: true, aborted: true }
acp: sessionUpdate agent_message_chunk "[OpenClaw interruption] session_status tool validation failed: invalid arguments"
acp: prompt settled → { stopReason: "cancelled" }
```

Also observed and now documented in the PR body: a client-initiated `session/cancel` settles the prompt locally in `cancelSessionWork` before the Gateway's aborted event arrives, so same-client cancels never show the notice (pre-existing `main` behavior). The abort-cause surface covers aborts originating outside the cancelling client — operator `/stop`, Control UI, another connection — which is the case where an unexpected cause needs explaining.

payload.author: Princeu3
payload.body:
All three findings are fixed, and the design changed rather than being patched around: the hangup decision now follows the observed outcome of that playback instead of a static provider capability.

**Do not hang up after failed final playback (P1)** — `handleInboundResponse` captures the `speak` result, logs and returns when it failed, and never reaches the hangup. Covered by `webhook.test.ts` "does not hang up when the closing reply failed to play".

**Do not infer end_call from malformed fallback text (P2)** — the inline fallback returns speech only; `endCall` is accepted solely from a successfully parsed object. Covered by "ignores an end_call flag in a reply that never parsed as JSON".

**Preserve caller control after a Twilio barge-in (P1)** — this was the right catch. `playTtsViaStream` returns early on `signal.aborted` before reaching the mark, so the old static check saw a configured stream and hung up on a caller who interrupted. `playTts` now returns `{ playback: "confirmed" | "unconfirmed" | "cancelled" }`, and `cancelled` keeps the line open. Verified live: the caller cut off the goodbye, the hangup was suppressed, and the conversation continued (trace in the PR body).

**Mark-timeout merge risk (P2)** — `sendMarkAndWait` now returns whether the carrier echoed the mark, so a local timeout resolves as `unconfirmed` and takes the grace path instead of being described as carrier-confirmed. Covered by a new `media-stream.playback-marks.test.ts` case.

The static `awaitsPlaybackCompletion` capability introduced in the first revision is gone.

736 tests pass; `pnpm build` and `pnpm check` are clean. The live traces cover the `cancelled` and `unconfirmed` branches; the `confirmed` branch is test-only because the installed release build sends the completion mark without awaiting the echo, and the PR body says so rather than implying otherwise.

The remaining item is the maintainer product decision on whether classic calls should have this action at all.

The deferred-parent-binding finding is not accepted: it treats an authorized repository choice as a perpetual grant from the parent. `InternalSessionEntry.pendingWorktree` is explicitly “Authorized worktree intent awaiting preparation by an admitted turn” (`src/config/sessions/types.ts:620`). Commit 54a53583565c (#131559) introduced that durable acceptance/retry boundary. Its preparation owner validates the exact current child session, admitted run/controller, lifecycle generation, pending intent, and calling runtime authority before binding; repository setup is authorized from the current caller, never the creator's saved privilege (`src/gateway/server-methods/session-create-project.ts:70`). The existing real-handler test “chat.send rechecks setup scope when a write-only caller retries an admin's failed worktree” demonstrates that a different authorized caller can resume the already-created session without inheriting admin setup authority (`src/gateway/server.sessions.create.projects.test.ts:464`).

Parent archive drains the parent's exact lifecycle identities and placement; it does not erase a durable child's accepted workspace choice (`src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-patch-archive.ts`, `src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-lifecycle-drain.ts`). Parent replacement/rebinding likewise does not revoke already-created session workspaces. The native sibling stores inherited workspace/cwd on the child for reuse on later turns (`src/config/sessions/types.ts:348`, `src/agents/subagents/spawn/subagent-spawn-session-patch.ts:124`). A durable parent binding would make operator retries fail according to whether checkout preparation happened just before or just after parent archival, contrary to that session-owned retry contract. The original caller still must remain live for its own privileged operations; this does not make copied runtime authority reusable.

Added production-path characterization uses real Gateway handlers, persisted session state, and real Git worktrees: after child acceptance, a real parent archive RPC, parent replacement, or parent worktree rebind leaves the child's authorized retry able to create its own checkout from the accepted repository. The child's identity and original lineage are preserved, repository setup remains disabled for operator.write, and the agent dispatch is reached. A fourth case replaces the child incarnation at workspace preparation and proves no repository lookup, checkout creation, or agent dispatch occurs. All four cases passed with the existing suite (12/12). The final patch replaces the old pending-only test with this stronger table, leaving 11 tests for exact-head CI; no behavior, schema, configuration, or protocol change was needed.

The source comment now states that source validation lasts through the child creation commit, and the managed-worktree docs explain the accepted child's retry ownership. The existing pending-worktree shape is unchanged; no durable parent grant is added. There is no production database schema change in this PR. The unrelated CI test-fixture extraction was dropped during rebase after main supplied its own repair.

payload.author: obviyus
payload.body:
Thanks @zhangguiping-xydt!

**Proof:** On Telegram Test Server, a direct message received `OPENCLAW_E2E_OK` after a forced lazy terminal-handler failure. Current main left the durable session `running` at the 70-second check; the repaired flow recorded it as `done`. Exact-head CI also passed.

- **Bug:** Optional chat presentation owned the durable terminal write, so a handler-load failure could leave a delivered turn marked `running`.
- **Fix:** The Gateway now starts the terminal write at the event subscription boundary, validates the live claim at commit, and prevents delayed starts from reopening terminal state.
- **Decision:** Accepted the production growth because it creates one claim-fenced persistence owner. Skipped separate Gateway-owner sign-off because no protected ownership rule applies; ClawSweeper found no defect, and independent review found no protected gate.

**Example**

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Telegram reply delivered; session still `running` after 70 seconds. | Telegram reply delivered; session is `done` after 70 seconds. |

I checked the tagged Crabbox sources behind the compatibility finding. The legacy-only shape is not a shipped dependency contract:

- [v0.41.1 provider matrix](https://github.com/openclaw/crabbox/blob/v0.41.1/internal/cli/providers.go#L13) and [v0.44.0 provider matrix](https://github.com/openclaw/crabbox/blob/v0.44.0/internal/cli/providers.go#L13) contain neither `classes` nor `classCatalog`. The intermediate v0.42.0 and v0.43.0 tags have the same absence. These binaries already return no advertised picker choices under the previous OpenClaw parser; the 0.41.1 runtime floor does not promise catalog metadata they never emitted.
- Legacy summaries were introduced by [65d9d8f7](https://github.com/openclaw/crabbox/commit/65d9d8f7937ec0d9b5da7826c161c46c569a3dac), then canonical profiles by [3b2420a6](https://github.com/openclaw/crabbox/commit/3b2420a6ce22c759b83703f592b883dc8d139566). Both first appear in v0.45.0. Comparing tags containing these two commits yields no tag that contains the legacy introduction without the canonical introduction.
- [v0.45.0 discovery](https://github.com/openclaw/crabbox/blob/v0.45.0/internal/cli/providers.go#L276) always writes `classCatalog`, with `classes` as an optional summary. Its [primary-profile projection](https://github.com/openclaw/crabbox/blob/v0.45.0/internal/cli/provider_classes.go#L132) already uses Linux/amd64 and positive integer GB/GiB, matching the inspected installed revision and this repair.

Disposition: the compatibility P1 and associated Rank-up move are not accepted. Adding a legacy fallback would preserve a brief untagged development state without an observed operator contract, while reintroducing the duplicate parser the repair deliberately removes. No supported tagged binary is shown to lose existing advertised choices; no version-floor or Doctor change is needed. The legacy-only fixture protects the canonical-authority boundary, not an upgrade promise.

The dependency-source proof gap in the automated review is covered by direct exact-revision and tagged-source inspection above, plus the real installed CLI/plugin/Gateway evidence already in the PR. No code changes, new tests, CI reruns, resource operations, or head changes were made in response. The exact-head CI and lead approval remain bound to `92946f78a0cc5963e19312070df62a717c6fe14c`.
