payload.author: steipete
payload.body:
The P1 was real and is fixed in `f7a028d`.

The item fetch passes `fetchGitHubApi` a `beforeRedirect` callback that re-asserts public visibility before following any redirect. I did not pass one on the new commits request, so a rename or transfer could have carried the operator's token into a repository it can read but the viewer cannot, and co-author data derived from that repository would have reached the browser. The pre-flight and post-flight visibility assertions do not cover it, because they check the original target rather than wherever the redirect points.

Rather than duplicate the callback, it is now a named local shared by every credentialed fetch in the module — the invariant is "any token-bearing request here re-checks visibility on redirect", and it should be impossible to add the next fetch without inheriting it.

`redirectedRepositoryApiUrl` also needed widening. It validated exactly the five-segment item path, so a commits redirect would have failed shape validation and been rejected. That is fail-closed and safe, but it would have silently dropped co-authors for every renamed repository. It now accepts the single known `commits` suffix and resolves to the same repository URL for the visibility check.

Regression coverage: a token-backed preview whose commits request 301s into a private repository. The test asserts the redirect target is visibility-checked, that no request is ever made to its commits URL, and that the card still renders with the co-author decoration withheld. Removing the guard fails it on the missing visibility check.

`node scripts/check-changed.mjs` is green, the preview suite passes at 21 tests, and Codex autoreview reports no findings on the fix.

payload.author: steipete
payload.body:
Also real, fixed in `9026545`.

The overflow was `total - coAuthors.length` — derived from people fetched rather than faces actually rendered. Avatar inlining is optional by design here (a failed or oversized avatar returns no data URL), so a co-author with no avatar rendered no face *and* was not counted in `+N`. Five co-authors with one failed avatar showed two faces and `+2`: four people represented, one silently gone. That is the silent-drop class, not a cosmetic off-by-one.

It now counts rendered faces, so the same case shows two faces and `+3`. When every avatar fails the stack degrades to a bare `+5` with the names still in the title, which is honest rather than empty.

The regression test asserts `+3` for exactly that shape and fails with `expected '+2' to be '+3'` against the previous arithmetic.

`node scripts/check-changed.mjs` is green, the card suite passes at 18 tests, and Codex autoreview reports no findings.

payload.author: steipete
payload.body:
Fair, and fixed in `73306a6`.

The faces are `alt=""` decorative images and the logins lived only in a `title`, which assistive tech does not reliably announce. That made the entire co-author signal sighted-only — the card told a screen reader nothing had changed. It is now one labelled image group carrying the same names, matching the `role="img"` + `aria-label` pattern already used for the sidebar's fork and status indicators.

The `title` stays for pointer users; the accessible name is what actually conveys the information. The test asserts the role, the accessible name, and that the individual faces remain decorative so a screen reader hears one summary rather than three empty images.

`node scripts/check-changed.mjs` is green, the card suite passes at 18 tests, and Codex autoreview reports no findings.

The attached recording is **after-only UI inspection** of the RPC-created synthetic session through normal masked-password login. The workspace chip exposes the canonical project path. Both the screenshot and decoded video frames were inspected before upload. The empty model picker is intentional: provider credentials and model turns were not needed for this admission-path proof. No operator state or service was touched.

Exact-head [CI run 33227095932](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/33227095932) passed on attempt 1, including the required `openclaw/ci-gate`. node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-methods/session-create-root.test.ts src/gateway/server.sessions.create.test.ts src/gateway/server.sessions.create.projects.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 --reporter=verbose

It preserves the separately landed directory validation, remote-node bypass, and caller-controlled worktree exemptions. Production LOC is net **-5**; tests are net **+211**.

Proof limits: native Windows and concurrent filesystem-replacement races were not exercised. The original failure is covered by the recorded pre-fix Gateway error, independent macOS before/after reproduction, and failing-then-passing regression cases; this recording is not presented as a before/after video or a demonstrated container escape.

payload.body:
### Deadline review disposition and native proof

The reported lost-`SIGTERM` deadline regression is not substantiated at `da4735ad82b9686fa51ef8b177dacb622f92ca40`. I inspected the complete current/base owners, callers, existing regression, Node's exit/close/kill implementation, and an independent before/after run using identical real Node fixtures. No production change is warranted for that mechanism.

Normal strict finalization already sends `SIGKILL` to any surviving owned group; if the group is gone, it joins inherited output. Cancellation during that join still owns the result. The base also treated timeout as “request termination, then join bounded cleanup”—not a promise to return at the exact timeout millisecond. See the [current finalizer and cancellation result](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/da4735ad82b9686fa51ef8b177dacb622f92ca40/scripts/lib/managed-child-process.mts#L418-L525) and the [base cleanup budget](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/7fc93d88013e7263cf6634c37efc5bf930e21ef7/scripts/lib/managed-child-process.mts#L441-L502).

Measured on Node 24.20.0/Darwin with a 1.5-second wall timeout; times include controller startup:

| Real fixture | Base | Published head |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Leader exits with an in-group output holder | `ETIMEDOUT`, 1.567s; holder receives TERM | Strict ownership failure, 0.143s; group receives KILL immediately |
| Escaped holder drains after 2.2s | `ETIMEDOUT`, 2.335s; both tails preserved | `ETIMEDOUT`, 2.336s; both tails preserved |
| Escaped holder never drains | Indeterminate cleanup failure, 11.534s | Same failure, 5.116s |
| Escaped holder drains before deadline | Success, 0.616s | Success, 0.636s |

In the escaped cases, the base's late group TERM returned `ESRCH`, and `child.kill("SIGTERM")` returned `false`: the holder was outside that target. Repeating those ineffective signals is not a repair.

The [existing combined regression](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/da4735ad82b9686fa51ef8b177dacb622f92ca40/test/scripts/managed-child-process.test.ts#L856-L952) already combines real leader exit, a dead owned group, open stdout/stderr, and deadline-before-closure. Its exact standalone controller passed both orderings on both revisions (4/4): `ETIMEDOUT` when the deadline precedes closure, success when closure precedes the deadline. This was standalone execution of the existing controller, not an additional Vitest invocation. The broader focused suite previously passed 100 tests with 43 Linux-only skips. All 38 process IDs recorded by the independent probes were confirmed absent after cleanup; no native app or operator store was accessed.

**Explicit policy decision:** strict normal-exit cleanup is bounded to five seconds after leader exit. A separate 6.2-second escaped-tail probe returned timeout with preserved tails on the base, but fails closed at 5.133s on the head. That distinction is intentional: a writer that remains outside the owned group beyond the drain budget does not earn a successful cleanup/cancellation result. Callers retain their resources on that failure. We accept this bounded-drain policy rather than reintroducing an unbounded wait, extending a timeout, or adding a parallel finalizer. This addresses the rank-up request without the proposed cancellation rewrite.

The other rank-up request is now satisfied: [exact-head native job 99078988909](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/33244280596/job/99078988909) passed **1,888 ordinary tests / 196 suites** and **both named AppState-isolation tests**, with all temporary diagnostics absent. The separate macOS Node lane stayed unassigned for over 20 minutes, so [hosted fallback 33245146940](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/33245146940) was dispatched for the same head before retiring the stalled run. Full CI is not yet claimed green; two hosted setup failures are being handled separately.

## ClawSweeper deletion-generation finding addressed

Fixed in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/b2d3fe70298e74eeafea2be0ab6ab7a707edccc6. The removed `sessionId` now comes from the actual delete/incognito-reset lifecycle result. The destructive UI merge checks the event's generation before removing anything; key-only lifecycle signals invalidate the roster rather than confirm deletion of its current occupant.

Both rank-up moves are covered: producer-owned identity and a failing-before delayed-delete-after-recreation regression. The focused shell cases cover subscription/direct delivery, identified/key-only events, and the absence of any prior local deletion. They preserve B's row, navigation, draft and queue, then prove a genuine B deletion still retires B. Real RPC-to-SQLite-to-emitter coverage recreates B before broadcast and proves the event retains A's identity without borrowing B's snapshot. Incognito reset and the dynamic lifecycle bridge are covered too.

**Fault-injected real-Gateway browser proof:** delete A, create B at the same key, wait for canonical B and enter a draft, then deliver A's actual deletion payload late. The delivery envelope keeps continuous sequence numbers to model delayed publication rather than packet loss. This distinction matters: an initial raw-frame hold triggered transport recovery and was not the reproduction. Before the fix, B vanished and navigation moved Home even though the server still held B. After the fix, the notification retains A's ID and B's row, navigation, and typed draft remain. The two attached videos show before and after; only idle setup was trimmed, and all media were inspected. Synthetic sessions only, with the proof session and dev Gateway cleaned up afterward.

payload.author: steipete
payload.body:
Addressing the incognito finding and both rank-up moves: I independently traced the candidate's producers and the pinned Codex source. I am **not accepting this as a reachable P1 in the supported flow**; restoring the old flag would reinstate a test-only path, not repair ordinary Codex-backed incognito forks.

The distinction is **Codex-backed** versus **upstream-linked**. [The Gateway selects native forking only when an upstream-link row exists](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/b2877cda37cdc9e76e95e916aa01657747f47acc/src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-rewind.ts#L357-L420). Without a link it uses [the local message-cut owner](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/b2877cda37cdc9e76e95e916aa01657747f47acc/src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-rewind.ts#L464). The caller cannot independently choose an incognito child: its storage class comes from the source. Ordinary Codex-backed incognito sessions take that local path; their real UI/provider flow, prefix, draft, child continuation, parent preservation, and reload passed. The real SQLite boundary tests additionally verify the absence of durable incognito rows and their loss on memory-store close.

Native catalog adoption [generates a deterministic durable harness key](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/b2877cda37cdc9e76e95e916aa01657747f47acc/extensions/codex/src/session-catalog-adoption.ts#L66) and [creates it without an incognito option](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/b2877cda37cdc9e76e95e916aa01657747f47acc/extensions/codex/src/session-catalog-adoption.ts#L358). The other production link writer is the native fork itself. Its [real runtime creator](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/b2877cda37cdc9e76e95e916aa01657747f47acc/src/plugins/runtime/runtime-agent.ts#L379-L433) does not forward incognito, and [the underlying creator rejects an incognito-shaped key without that flag](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/b2877cda37cdc9e76e95e916aa01657747f47acc/src/gateway/session-create-service.ts#L436-L442). Patch, alias, migration, and binding-import paths did not supply a supported linked-incognito producer. The removed mock changed only the child key on a durable-source fixture and replaced this real creator.

For the dependency-source rank-up: I personally read sibling Codex at `rust-v0.150.1`, commit [`90854393966b21e9ebfd21b122334eb09a20c93d`](https://github.com/openai/codex/tree/90854393966b21e9ebfd21b122334eb09a20c93d). An omitted [fork `ephemeral` flag does default to false](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/90854393966b21e9ebfd21b122334eb09a20c93d/codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/thread.rs#L584-L585), so the review's *conditional* storage concern is valid. But that version [rejects `thread/turns/list` for ephemeral threads](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/90854393966b21e9ebfd21b122334eb09a20c93d/codex-rs/app-server/src/request_processors/thread_processor.rs#L3438-L3442), and [our handler requires that read before the native fork](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/b2877cda37cdc9e76e95e916aa01657747f47acc/extensions/codex/src/app-server/upstream-fork-boundary.ts#L238). Merely linking a genuine ephemeral thread therefore cannot reach the alleged write either.

Qualification: trusted plugins have broad SDK mutation capabilities; I am not claiming they cannot manually manufacture inconsistent state. I found no documented supported producer or shipped migration contract for the state alleged here. A concrete such path would change this disposition. The ephemeral-restoration rank-up is skipped for that reason; pinned dependency inspection is complete. Durable original-source forks, including repeated creation and continuation after a Gateway/app-server restart, also passed live.

Separately, CI identified a type-only barrel cycle and stale generated prompt fixtures. Those are being corrected; this comment is not a claim that the PR is ready to merge before CI is green.

payload.author: steipete
payload.body:
The required-resolver decision was made before implementation and is recorded in the [maintainer-approved bounded design](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/132126). The approved scope includes a **required allocation-only resolver**, migration of Crabbox, paired-device and static-SSH producers together, and no teardown fallback into provisioning. This is the intended unshipped SDK cutover: prerelease providers missing the method must update before registration succeeds. Latest stable `v2026.7.1-2` predates this worker-provider API; no stable provider contract is being silently removed. No new transition/compatibility path is requested or added. This addresses the decision and Rank-up item in the latest review without reopening the already approved choice.

The storage change is the approved timing/ownership change within existing fields and the existing provisioning-to-draining representation, not a new schema/table/column/state/version. The linked issue records that material-persistence approval and the rollback caveat; schema compatibility alone is not a claim that the old provisioning-replay behavior is safe.

The latest review is now for `11c45558c457d1a8bc73a7daac65a6bdf667d1bd`; its required-contract/Rank-up decision remains covered by that prior explicit approval, not a new inferred approval. Latest stable was rechecked on August 29 UTC and is still `v2026.7.1-2`.

Production growth is **+96/-47, net +49**, with **+525/-94 tests/test support** and **+6/-4 docs**. This is the bounded new cleanup-identity capability and its ownership boundary: required public contract, three actual producer implementations, validation of untyped identity results, and current-owner checks around awaited publication/teardown. The implementation removes both calls from cleanup back into provisioning and the obsolete late-bootstrap skip. Reusing `provision` with a mode flag, an optional resolver/fallback, or fabricated transport fields would retain the ownership defect rather than absorb it. Existing stop/destroy and store transitions are reused; there is no parallel teardown owner. The CI fencing follow-through adds no net executable production statements—only two invariant-comment lines. The provider boundary is the concrete reason this coherent repair has positive production LOC.

CI did catch a real local-fencing order regression in the first candidate. The corrected owner fences cached authority before provider lookup/resolution; 404 distinct owner/producer/sibling tests passed, including shared/unknown-host ACK requirements and bound unreported nodes. The startup fixture now waits on allocation resolution rather than the intentionally removed provision replay. The correction is published, fresh restricted P0 autoreview is clean, full changed checks/build/package validation passed, and exact-head [CI run 33231203001](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/33231203001) is green. The inherited checkout fixture fixes were taken from their canonical main repairs, without weakening assertions or deadlines.

This is **not yet a land-ready claim**: matching-package live acceptance and native review/prepare/merge remain in progress. The body distinguishes historical scoped no-create/repeat/restart proof from the later real allocated-VM failure/cleanup proof, and records the experimental-backend, key-mismatch and real-Chrome UI limitations. Contributor-gate labeling does not waive those limits.

## Pre-merge review resolution and proof

Reviewed head: `d2355a8aba090008814eaf5c239490a216fba907`.

The latest [ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/132210#issuecomment-5458954041) correctly notes that the upstream `rolldown-plugin-dts` 0.28.2 engine declaration excludes Node 25. That metadata is **not** being rewritten or described as fixed. The maintainer landing decision is to retain the explicitly selected, age-qualified 0.28.2 release, keep OpenClaw's runtime engine declaration unchanged, and accept the documented upstream build-tool support gap. Node 24 and 26 remain the upstream-supported build paths; strict-engine Node 25 installation is not claimed as supported by this package.

There is now direct **Node 25.9.0** execution proof for the changed declaration path, using the published 0.28.2 artifact and tsdown 0.22.14:

| Scenario | Observed result |
| --- | --- |
| Healthy native declarations | Build exits 0 and emits the expected declaration |
| Malformed TypeScript | Native compiler reports TS1109, exits 2, and emits partial output; enclosing build exits 1 and preserves the previous declaration byte-for-byte |
| Compiler self-termination by SIGTERM | Enclosing build exits 1 with the signal diagnostic and preserves the previous declaration byte-for-byte |

The checked-in regression also passes on Node 25.9.0:

```bash
fnm exec --using 25.9.0 -- node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/tsdown-build.test.ts -t 'preserves successful declarations when the native compiler fails'
```

**Rank-up disposition:** the requested Node 25 declaration-build result is supplied. Selecting a different upstream release solely to change its engine declaration is skipped for this landing in favor of the approved 0.28.2 fix; no new dependency patch, engine override, or relaxed validation is introduced. The upstream source-inspection gap in the automated review is covered by direct inspection of the integrity-verified published package, including its exit/signal rejection, plus these executed boundary probes. This is evidence for the affected flow, not a claim that every Node 25 installation mode or unrelated build path was tested.

The compiler fix stays at its upstream process owner. The associated npm projection repair uses npm's canonical `"."` self-pin shape, preserving parent and child constraints in either input order without weakening alias/conflict checks. All 94 npm lock validations and the portable plugin-staging regression pass. The inherited UI shard failure is already repaired through the merged main-branch fix; no cap increase or duplicate UI change was added here.

[Exact-head CI run 33225040194](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/33225040194) completed successfully: 168 successful jobs, 16 workflow-skipped jobs, no failures. The required `openclaw/ci-gate` is successful from GitHub Actions app 15368. Live effective main rules require that check and linear history; they do not require an independent approval. Secops ownership is satisfied by the requesting maintainer's active team membership.

Fresh independent Codex autoreview of the complete six-file PR is scoped-clean at its default P0 threshold, with no accepted/actionable findings. It explicitly retains the upstream Node 25 metadata/strict-install caveat rather than treating runtime proof as a metadata fix.

**Direct Darwin-contract evidence:** five independently owned child processes were started in new sessions, retained without reaping, and checked to be `Z` with matching parent/PID/group identity. Redacted terminal results:

```text
owned group state: Z
signal 0 -> PermissionError(errno=1)     5/5
SIGTERM  -> PermissionError(errno=1)     5/5
SIGKILL  -> PermissionError(errno=1)     5/5
all five children subsequently reaped by their owning test parent
```

A separate original-order canonical run captured this exception chain:

```text
initial:   group_alive -> os.killpg(pgid, 0) -> PermissionError(errno=1)
secondary: drain error path -> group_signal(SIGKILL) -> PermissionError(errno=1)
owner exit: 125; no further checkout reuse
```

I directly inspected the published [Darwin traversal](https://github.com/apple-oss-distributions/xnu/blob/main/bsd/kern/kern_sig.c#L1642-L1721). Its explicit-group filter excludes `SZOMB`, and the zero-eligible-target result can be `EPERM`. The native probe proves the observed host behavior; I am not assuming that source identifies the exact running kernel build or retroactively attributing the original uninstrumented incident.

**Fail-closed proof:** the deterministic regression failed first on the old owner’s zombie-group probe and then, after that repair, on the fixture counting a held zombie as live. The repaired regression passes and verifies that an actually live owned group whose signal is denied still raises. Failed inspection remains fatal. A leader-only temporary owner is still rejected by the repaired observer at five live-descendant boundaries, followed by clean fixture lease teardown. The +7 workflow lines preserve the original deadline and missing-group fast path; they do not blindly ignore permission errors.

Local final verification:

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/ci-platform-checkout.test.ts
```

21/21 passed on macOS, including the original 20-case order. All active-descendant boundaries were empty and every sentinel remained alive.

```bash

```

```bash
pnpm check:workflows
```

Both passed. Fresh isolated Codex autoreview was scoped-clean at its default P0 threshold. The checked owner, test, fixture, and PID-helper hashes were unchanged by the publication rebase.

**CI is land-ready:** [run 33222200085](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/33222200085) succeeded on exact head `5aa57199b90eda3abb1fc365f42d8fd70ae61896`, with no failed jobs and both native Windows jobs passing. The first [run 33221011275](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/33221011275) had passed Windows but failed an inherited UI type-root overflow (724 above the unchanged 720 cap). The mechanical rebase incorporated the already-landed [main partition fix](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/249c248285b03eacc1fdcb9153bc47c6c3a2ec20): pages 419, E2E 305, other 412, with complete coverage and the same cap. `pnpm lint:tmp:tsgo-core-boundary` and `pnpm tsgo:test:ui` also pass locally. No limit was increased, no checkout bytes changed in that rebase, and no gate is bypassed.

The separate four-second cancellation-readiness startup ceiling under contention remains an explicit follow-up. The transient PID survivor that disappeared before state capture is not retroactively labeled a zombie.

The P1 does not reproduce on the reviewed head f099013a41f86cd65f7ce8b37a5c36da16033caa.

I reran the exact stale-partial browser fixture:

    node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.ui-e2e.config.ts --configLoader runner ui/src/e2e/dashboard-final-reply-recovery.e2e.test.ts

Result: 1/1 passed. The fixture already asserts that the stale unmarked final_answer partial causes a second chat.history read and that exactly one durable final appears.

The metadata-divergence premise is false because terminalReplyDisplaySignature serializes safeNormalizeMessage(message).content. normalizeMessage converts the raw text block to its display shape and does not retain cache_control, so the live partial and stale partial produce the same signature. Recovery therefore continues to the second read.

I made no code change because the proposed failure was falsified by the exact behavior contract. Please re-review the unchanged head.

payload.author: steipete
payload.body:
Verified pre-merge boundary finding on `8f7528f014d996fece503c93c8abdaa9f3e857bd`: **cancellation during timeout cleanup is reported as retryable timeout in the new raw `--git` path.**

In [`run_git`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/8f7528f014d996fece503c93c8abdaa9f3e857bd/.github/workflows/ci.yml#L398-L414), `FetchTimeout` is raised before `finally` drains the process group. If SIGTERM arrives during that drain, the handler latches cancellation, but the pending exception skips the trailing `check_cancelled()`. The [raw CLI mapper](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/8f7528f014d996fece503c93c8abdaa9f3e857bd/.github/workflows/ci.yml#L538-L547) then exits 124. This matters because the [npm-lock continuation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/8f7528f014d996fece503c93c8abdaa9f3e857bd/.github/workflows/ci.yml#L3066-L3081) treats 143 as terminal but permits the full-sweep fallback for 124.

Native Linux proof executed the exact extracted owner with `--git 1`, leaving its real ten-second cleanup allowance unchanged. Fake Git forked a real child and grandchild in the inherited group; the observer sent SIGTERM to the owner only after a child had recorded the first timeout-drain TERM, rather than after a guessed sleep.

| Case | Owner exit | Tree dead before return | Unrelated sentinel |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- |
| Original owner, SIGTERM during drain | **124 (wrong)** | Yes | Alive |
| Original owner, SIGTERM before deadline | 143 | Yes | Alive |
| Scratch-only owner ordering repair, during drain | 143 | Yes | Alive |
| Scratch-only repair, before deadline | 143 | Yes | Alive |

Original extracted Python SHA-256: `60bdd208580519fe2acbbf7de511894908c9cdbe267b7b335b85076fdafb1b2e`. The successful observations used an isolated cached Node Bookworm container with `--init --network none`; no real Git network, credentials, repository mutations, or unrelated process signals. Cleanup and status were asserted separately. An initial fixture-only bind-mount lease failure was discarded as inconclusive, not counted as product evidence.

Please preserve the canonical ordering **verified drain → cancellation decision → timeout/Git result**, with cleanup uncertainty still terminal and higher priority. Repair it once in the owner, not with another npm-lock status guard. The scratch fix demonstrates the ordering but is not presented as landed code or complete review of setup-error precedence. Add the during-drain regression before merging; the outside-CI owner extraction will reuse the corrected primitive rather than fork it.

payload.author: obviyus
payload.body:
Thanks @ruel225!

**Proof:** On exact current-main baseline `5d3bd15130a`, an isolated Gateway showed the final reply, committed one same-run SQLite row, then recorded a second abort-marked row after a late `chat.abort`. On exact head `d96e279fec1`, the same scenario kept one row before abort, one row after abort, zero abort-marked duplicates, and one row after closing and reopening SQLite.

- **Bug:** A completed reply could remain in the live buffer and be persisted again when a late abort arrived during delayed settlement.
- **Fix:** Abort persistence now checks the same run and reply inside the SQLite commit transaction, so synchronous terminal writers cannot race between the check and insert.

**Example**

| Before | After |

| History contains the completed reply and a duplicate abort-marked copy. | History keeps one completed reply and no duplicate abort row. |

Thanks @ayaangazali for tracking down and documenting the real CI failure. Closing this as superseded by the now-passing main build rather than adding an unnecessary baseline increase.

I verified an **uncached production artifact build** of main [5b605da389460fd035d9a2031064ed949303b14f](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/5b605da389460fd035d9a2031064ed949303b14f): [CI run 33213197214 / build-artifacts job 98993434045](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/33213197214/job/98993434045). The log shows the exact-revision dist cache miss, `pnpm build:ci-artifacts`, 774 verified compressed sidecars, and the actual size check:

```text
startup JS gzip: 345124 B
current baseline: 347255 B
current enforcement limit: 347831 B
ui:build completed successfully
```

That measurement is **1,913 B below the original 347,037 B limit** that prompted this PR, not just below the newer limit. Main already records the tighter 347,255 B baseline from [#132020 — compact mobile session actions](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/132020). This PR would raise it another 168 B to 347,423 B, but the measured current bundle does not need that additional allowance.

The source comparison and an independent check of the actual build log confirm that the reported artifact-size failure is resolved without this baseline-only patch. The existing growth/variance rules and maximum committed baseline are unchanged. This conclusion is scoped to the startup-size gate; it is not a claim that every unrelated CI job is green, nor an attribution of the entire size reduction to one commit.

Both P2 findings were real and are fixed in `1877a57`.

**Rate-limit fallback.** Correct, and worse than a dropped field: the path rebuilt each chip from a hand-written literal that duplicated the one in `finishPullRequest`, so the author disappeared precisely when the UI was already degraded, despite having come from the list fetch that had already succeeded. Both callers now share `stateOnlyPullRequestChip`, so the shape cannot drift again. The existing rate-limit test carries an author now instead of gaining a near-duplicate sibling.

**Authorless row grid.** Also correct, and my original code comment asserted the opposite — I claimed an `auto` column preserved the old layout. It does not: each PR row is its own grid container, so omitting the cell moved the diff stats out of the trailing `1fr` column and killed the flush-right alignment. The cell is now always emitted, empty for a ghosted account.

That finding also exposed a flaw in my evidence. The "before" screenshot in the original PR body had reverted only the component while keeping the new CSS, so it showed authorless rows misaligned in a way `main` never was — I had looked at that image and passed it. The PR body now carries a corrected pair captured against the parent commit with both the component and the stylesheet reverted, and calls out the earlier mistake. Rows #418–#420 are identical across the corrected shots, which is the property the second finding was asking for.

`node scripts/check-changed.mjs` is green (the fix first tripped `no-map-spread`, resolved by the shared-helper extraction rather than a suppression), and the gateway, component, and E2E suites pass.

Maintainer verification update for [eec0cbc6d216d382ab72821988d3213151f64474](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/eec0cbc6d216d382ab72821988d3213151f64474): **the repair is verified locally and exact-head CI is green, but I have not landed it because the requested packaged Parallels proof is blocked before OpenClaw runs.**

Completed proof:

- The full owner/sibling command passed 107 tests:
  ```bash
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/update-runner.test.ts src/infra/update-package-manager.test.ts src/cli/update-cli/progress.test.ts
  ```
- The complete changed-file gate, formatting, and diff checks passed. The committed patch is byte-identical to the independently reviewed patch; Codex autoreview reported no actionable findings at its default P0 threshold.
- Full `pnpm build`, Control UI build, canonical package acceptance, and the matching Codex plugin artifact completed successfully. Core tarball SHA256: `e0a55d02025b4659555a88df6efaa94c50501f31694846eab343625e8af821e7`; both artifacts identify the exact candidate above.
- [Exact-head CI run 33208555193](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/33208555193) is green.

The Ubuntu fixture retained its original **3,878,404,096-byte `/tmp` tmpfs** while exposing real 12 GB RAM, with no guest `TMPDIR` or heap override. Admission verified a separate disk-backed root filesystem and preservation of the unrelated existing checkout. However, the run stopped while creating the private transport directory, before package installation or the installed updater command.

The failure is reproducible independently of OpenClaw: identical no-op Node and `chmod` commands intermittently fail through Parallels 27 with exit 255 and `PrlJob_GetRetCode` / `PrlJob_GetResult: Invalid argument`. A bounded comparison failed 1/12 default-terminal probes and 2/12 advanced-terminal probes. The vendor's matching 27.0.0 tools were then installed successfully in a separate transient guest service; the same SDK failure recurred after six successful probes. Consequently, neither terminal selection nor the tools-version mismatch is established as a repair. No product retry, timeout increase, or weakened assertion was used to call this a pass.

Ubuntu has been restored to the original snapshot, 8192 MB, stopped, with its original virtual media configuration. Task artifact servers were stopped. No packaged after-fix success or post-merge retest is claimed; reliable guest execution remains required before landing.

ClawSweeper follow-through: exact-head CI is now complete; packaged default/redirect traces remain unfulfilled rather than silently skipped. Redirected storage already has real-Git owner-boundary coverage. Production remains net +20 lines, with no further growth. The stored-data heuristic attached to `src/cli/update-cli/progress.ts` is a false positive: those six added lines return CLI recovery text; this patch has no persistence or schema migration.

Its two small files are written only under the verifier's newly created synthetic HOME, which the existing outer `finally` removes. **Persist provenance in active Copilot steering (P2) + both P1 merge risks — fixed.** The Copilot steering branch now routes `session.send` through a new `transcriptJournal.sendSdkUser` seam: a deferred gate is scheduled into the journal's serialized queue *before* the SDK dispatch, so a `user.message` event that arrives ahead of the send response still queues behind the messageId→recorder binding (no FIFO guessing, safe for concurrent steers). `recordSdkUser` then stamps the recorder's `provenance` onto the SDK-built row — the SDK idempotency key stays authoritative (no duplicate rows), the recorder is satisfied via `markRuntimePersisted`/`markRuntimePersistencePending` rather than a second write, and suppressed writes mark the recorder blocked so the `waitForTranscriptCommit` receipt contract holds. Regression tests drive real SDK events in both orderings (event before and after the send response) and assert the persisted row carries `kind: inter_session` provenance exactly once with a confirmed receipt.

Sibling sweep across runtimes consuming the steering recorder: Codex app-server persists recorder-bearing items (fixed earlier in this PR, `extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt-active-turn.ts`); Copilot fixed here; no other runtime persists an SDK-built user row on an active-steering path, so no further repairs were needed.

**Sibling-Codex inspection (P1).** The repository gate was satisfied by the acting agent directly: `../codex/codex-rs/app-server/src/request_processors/turn_processor.rs:505-575` (turn/steer maps input items to turn `UserInput` tagged with `client_user_message_id`), `message_processor.rs:1377` (TurnSteer dispatch), and `app-server-protocol/src/protocol/common.rs` (method registration) were read in the sibling checkout. The PR's Codex-extension change is protocol-neutral: it does not alter any wire interaction, only which OpenClaw-side items commit their transcript recorder at the already-confirmed consumption point. ClawSweeper's read-only environment lacks `../codex`, which is why it could not verify this itself.

**Stored data model flag.** False positive: no durable schema changes. `worker-session-tool-executor.ts` adds a call argument, `sessions-send-tool.ts` writes standard transcript events through the existing recorder, and `chat-thread-items.ts` is a display-side dedup signature. `PersistedUserTurnMessage.provenance` in `user-turn-transcript.types.ts` only makes an already-persisted runtime field visible to types.

All three P1 findings are addressed at `f63eca4c`:

1. **Authoritative row only** — the outcome now commits through `commitCronRuntimeRows` (row reread under the SQLite write lock, single-row upsert) instead of the full-store `persist()`, and applies back via `applyCronRuntimeRowsToState`.

payload.body:
Finding addressed — and it was a fair hit.

The renamed test asserted the *returned* entry lacked both fields, which merge-base also satisfies by parsing both documents and deleting them afterwards. It protected the output, not the optimization.

It now asserts the mechanism: the test captures the JSON handed to `parseSessionEntryJson` and proves

- a **cold** list load (`readConsistency: "latest"`, which bypasses the snapshot cache) receives documents containing neither `skillsSnapshot` nor `systemPromptReport`;
- an **incremental revalidation** — forced by an untracked same-connection `INSERT` of a row that *does* carry both documents — also receives stripped JSON for the re-read row;
- a **full** read still receives both, so a later change cannot quietly strip the full path too.

Verified it discriminates: with production files reverted to the merge-base, it fails with

```
cold list load: expected '{"sessionId":"lazy-list-projection",…' not to contain 'skillsSnapshot'
```

Writing it surfaced something worth recording: the first attempt asserted *zero* parses on the cold read and failed, because a tracked upsert patches both caches in place without parsing. That is correct behaviour, and it is why reaching the genuinely cold path needs `readConsistency: "latest"`.

Local validation on this head: `check:changed` clean, `src/config/sessions` 95 files / 1066 tests, and `server.sessions.list-store-materialization.test.ts` 7/7 (the malformed-row guard).

**Published artifact identity:** [npm 0.1.19](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@openclaw/crabline/v/0.1.19), published `2026-08-28T17:29:46.734Z`; [registry tarball](https://registry.npmjs.org/@openclaw/crabline/-/crabline-0.1.19.tgz). ```

The npm provenance binds that exact digest to `openclaw/crabline`, `.github/workflows/release.yml`, tag `v0.1.19`, and commit [`08e609fc567566100460e738033f8af66b0db141`](https://github.com/openclaw/crabline/commit/08e609fc567566100460e738033f8af66b0db141). No tag movement, package replacement, or source workaround was used.

Ancestors accept only ACL-free or fully understood non-propagating deny entries; private storage remains ACL-free. Granting, mixed, propagating, malformed, unknown, or unverifiable ACLs fail closed, including ACLs masked by the `@` xattr marker. Independent POSIX ownership/write-mode and sticky-boundary checks remain intact. OpenClaw's repo-relative output-root contract is unchanged; relocating artifacts or duplicating the dependency's validator would be the wrong repair layer.

**Observed macOS behavior:** Darwin 25.6.0, Node 24.20.0, umask `022`. The original missing/existing-parent scenarios under the actual unchanged home ACL reject on 0.1.17 and pass on installed 0.1.19. Seven additional inheritance/permission/parser scenarios passed against the unchanged ACL classifier. Home ACL/mode/UID/inode stayed unchanged; owned fixtures were removed. Foreign-owner rejection was inspected in source, not runtime-tested with `chown`; Linux CI is not substituted for this native macOS proof.

The intervening 0.1.18 cancellation bug was independently reproduced and repaired in [Crabline #286 — contain recorder rejections during WhatsApp shutdown](https://github.com/openclaw/crabline/pull/286), before adoption. The [shared waiter](https://github.com/openclaw/crabline/blob/08e609fc567566100460e738033f8af66b0db141/src/servers/whatsapp-baileys-websocket.ts#L183-L204) observes already-started work before checking pre-abortion. Maintainer review complete for `c51e7f614379ab2176a2005a7dd2480ba85fac44`; ready for the repository-native prepare/merge checks.

The root cause is an Android client contract left behind after #131233: the retired retry could emit a field excluded by the closed Gateway schema, and the ordinary review dialog still promised that retry. Ordinary installs already omitted the flag. Removing the request/state/UI path at the Android owners is the canonical fix; restoring a server flag or adding compatibility would preserve the obsolete contract rather than repair it.

Exact source references, detail-reviewed versions, install-only version omission, route/generation/operation/admin guards, timeouts and readback remain intact. Both successful audit warnings and rejected error-detail warnings remain readable. Server production code and the separate operator install policy are unchanged.

**Proof:** [CI run 33202426523](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/33202426523) is successful on this exact head, including Play/ThirdParty/Wear tests, phone and Wear debug builds/lint, `android-ktlint`, native localization, security checks, and [the required `openclaw/ci-gate`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/33202426523/job/98959209370). The earlier run found Kotlin formatting issues; the follow-up changes are whitespace-only. Local `:app:ktlintCheck` also passes with the verified Java 21 toolchain.

Additional local commands completed:

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-methods/skills.clawhub.test.ts
```

```bash
pnpm native:i18n:verify
```

```bash
node scripts/check-native-state-schema-version.mjs
```

```bash
git diff --check
```

The Gateway suite passed 18 tests. The original and cleaned-up Kotlin-emitted requests were independently checked against the actual Gateway validator without invoking an install; 16 isolated Kotlin helper/error tests also passed. The exact nine-path changed gate passed with pinned tools. Fresh independent review of the complete formatted patch reported no actionable P0 findings.

### Late compatibility review decision

The [late ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/132016#issuecomment-5456375121) raises the older-Gateway acknowledgement scenario. That server scenario is real, but the claimed stable Android upgrade obligation is not established: the Android flow was introduced by [84fb7a664d6b / #101864](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/84fb7a664d6bf599bc25f18a7087a5a8d9420be5), whose reachable version tags are prereleases only. The live latest stable release is [v2026.7.1-2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/releases/tag/v2026.7.1-2), commit `0790d9f593ad30c940ed93b5872a8cf6d6f3cf8c`; its Android tree has no `SkillManagement.kt`, `installClawHubSkill`, or acknowledgement path. Its Gateway does retain the older field, which is why this interoperability case must be described rather than denied.

Maintainer decision: retain the explicitly requested current-contract cleanup, not legacy acknowledgement compatibility. For this updated Android ClawHub workflow, use a Gateway build containing [the #131233 audit contract](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/7b7858d9552fcfb1e4d1cff80ad214f4ae79313c). An older Gateway that requests the retired acknowledgement must be updated to complete that case; the error/warning remains visible. This is not a claim that ordinary installs against older Gateways all fail, and no stable version number is invented for the unreleased contract.

Retaining the legacy retry or adding a capability/version compatibility path is intentionally declined under the requested retirement and the repository's stable-tag compatibility policy. payload.author: steipete
payload.body:
Accepted the malformed-value finding — it was a real hole and it's fixed in `1bc90c2`.

`isGitCoauthorCreditEnabled` now reads `value === undefined || value === true`, so a missing row is still the default (credit on) but anything else, including the arbitrary JSON `users.prefs.set` will happily persist, fails closed rather than publishing a verified person's public trailer. Regression coverage lands at both readers: the attribution resolver test gains a `malformed` participant whose stored `"yes"` keeps it out of the trailers and the `Worked on by` list, and the profile page regains malformed-value coverage as a dedicated test rather than the fixture line this PR had repurposed.

On the remaining rank-up moves:

- **Real Gateway-to-commit evidence for absent vs explicit-false.** Covering both states at the owner boundary instead: `src/agents/git-coauthor-attribution.test.ts` asserts the exact emitted `Co-authored-by` trailers and `Worked on by` list for an absent row (credited), an explicit `false` (omitted), and now a malformed row (omitted). That is the commit-facing output of the changed predicate. The Control UI side has real-browser before/after screenshots from the mocked-gateway E2E lane in the PR body. A live gateway-to-commit run would be stronger evidence, and I'm not claiming it as done.
- **Maintainer direction for flipping unconfigured profiles to default-on.** This PR was requested directly by the repository owner; the default flip is the intended product change, not an incidental side effect. Documented in `docs/concepts/user-model.md`, `docs/concepts/multi-user.md`, and `docs/web/control-ui.md`.

payload.author: steipete
payload.body:
Resolved the P1 with maintainer direction, and the direction was that the rule was being read too broadly.

`VISION.md`'s privacy sentence governs what leaves an install — telemetry to the project. It is not a statement about shared Gateways: on `team.openclaw.ai`, where OpenClaw is built with OpenClaw and visitors are sometimes invited, the people you share a Gateway with see the work you do there, and Git co-author credit exists precisely to attribute that work to the human who did it. Default-on credit for a *verified* account on a *shared* session is that policy working, not a violation of it.

Rather than assert that reading, `6ece951` writes it down. `VISION.md` now states the personal-and-team direction up front, and the privacy rule says explicitly what it covers ("telemetry attribution to the project") and what it does not. That removes the ambiguity that produced this finding instead of leaving the next review to hit the same wall.

The other half of the finding was fair and is fixed: an absent preference no longer means "any value goes". Only a missing row or literal `true` enables credit, so malformed persisted JSON fails closed.

### Inspectable live Gateway proof

Re-run against the exact PR head `0b187489af973a4a38a841d9dd1a8d84b35d50ec` (`OpenClaw 2026.8.1 (0b18748)`). Both runs used disposable loopback Gateways with isolated config/state; no production config, state, port, or process was modified. Both Gateways were stopped cleanly after the run. Paths, machine identifiers, connection IDs, and local auth details are omitted.

#### 1. Real Claude CLI runtime across a full refresh

The isolated agent explicitly mapped both configured Anthropic models to `agentRuntime.id = claude-cli`. The following is the redacted command output; each line is the filtered result of a real `models.list` Gateway RPC.

```text
$ models.list agent=main preparedOnly=true
[{"ref":"anthropic/claude-opus-5","runtime":"claude-cli","available":true},{"ref":"anthropic/claude-sonnet-5","runtime":"claude-cli","available":true}]

$ models.list agent=main
[{"ref":"anthropic/claude-opus-5","runtime":"claude-cli","available":true},{"ref":"anthropic/claude-sonnet-5","runtime":"claude-cli","available":true}]

$ models.list agent=main view=all refresh=true
[{"ref":"anthropic/claude-opus-5","runtime":"claude-cli","available":true},{"ref":"anthropic/claude-sonnet-5","runtime":"claude-cli","available":true}]

$ models.list agent=main preparedOnly=true
[{"ref":"anthropic/claude-opus-5","runtime":"claude-cli","available":true},{"ref":"anthropic/claude-sonnet-5","runtime":"claude-cli","available":true}]

$ models.list agent=main
[{"ref":"anthropic/claude-opus-5","runtime":"claude-cli","available":true},{"ref":"anthropic/claude-sonnet-5","runtime":"claude-cli","available":true}]

$ agent agent=main message="Reply with exactly OK" deliver=false
{"status":"ok","text":"OK","provider":"claude-cli","model":"claude-opus-5"}
```

This covers startup/prepared state, the ordinary model view, an explicit full catalog refresh, both post-refresh views, and a real native Claude turn.

#### 2. Direct-route and sibling-runtime isolation through a real Gateway

For an inspectable auth-scope trace, a second disposable Gateway loaded one local no-network fixture plugin. It declared two synthetic runtime IDs, `proof-selected-runtime` and `proof-sibling-runtime`. Its discovery hook only appended the exact `provider` argument passed to `resolveSyntheticAuth`; it returned a non-secret fixture value only for those two declared IDs. The probe file was cleared before each RPC.

```text
$ models.list agent=selected view=all refresh=true
synthetic auth probes: ["proof-selected-runtime"]

$ models.list agent=direct view=all refresh=true
synthetic auth probes: []

$ models.list agent=sibling view=all refresh=true
synthetic auth probes: ["proof-sibling-runtime"]
```

Thus the full refresh projects the exact selected runtime, does not probe a native runtime for a direct provider route, and does not leak the selected runtime into the sibling agent (or vice versa).

Addressed the source-verification item and rank-up move in the latest ClawSweeper review. I personally inspected both upstream checkouts; no runtime or wording change was needed.

- Codex `rust-v0.150.1` resolves to `0eb410ad0dd161ea323b05452f978de01cd63430`. Its [native tool registration](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/0eb410ad0dd161ea323b05452f978de01cd63430/codex-rs/core/src/tools/spec_plan.rs#L1099) registers `apply_patch` when the environment and model support it, without applying OpenClaw-managed tool omission. This is a tool-visibility distinction, not a claim that read-only execution permits writes. OpenClaw separately supplies the native permission policy in [session-permission-policy.ts](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/47c7a081caac6ec1ddf5750a615ed66c89316d8f/extensions/codex/src/app-server/session-permission-policy.ts).
- Hermes `306db2776c6b6f1acc85c31c4dabba3263f0e9fd`: [local dispatch](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/306db2776c6b6f1acc85c31c4dabba3263f0e9fd/tools/code_execution_tool.py#L1634) and [kernel-mode resolution](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/306db2776c6b6f1acc85c31c4dabba3263f0e9fd/tools/code_execution_tool.py#L2070) use persistent local kernels and ignore the retired setting. The executable [remote dispatch](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/306db2776c6b6f1acc85c31c4dabba3263f0e9fd/tools/code_execution_tool.py#L1273) attempts a persistent kernel, then falls back to per-call execution when unavailable. This executable path supersedes a stale adjacent comment saying remote execution is only per-call.
- Hermes [remote keys](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/306db2776c6b6f1acc85c31c4dabba3263f0e9fd/tools/code_kernel_remote.py#L161) include task identity; [reset and reuse](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/306db2776c6b6f1acc85c31c4dabba3263f0e9fd/tools/code_kernel_remote.py#L327) use an in-memory registry and discard the old kernel on reset. [Task creation](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/306db2776c6b6f1acc85c31c4dabba3263f0e9fd/run_agent.py#L8630) supplies a new UUID when no task ID is passed. The addendum therefore does not promise restoration across a parent restart or a new task identity.

This is pinned source verification, not a live or adversarial Hermes certification. Ordinary backup payload hashing remains separate work in #118125.

Exact live symlink-alias regression proof at current PR HEAD `a73e12fe60445900f242290a4e799135517098e4`.

Environment:

- OpenClaw source build: `2026.8.1 (a73e12f)`
- Installed OpenShell: `0.0.106`
- Local mTLS OpenShell gateway with Podman compute
- No model or provider credentials used

Scenario:

1. Created one physical host workspace and a symlink alias with a different lexical path but the same realpath.
2. Created and prewarmed two distinct OpenShell mirror runtimes with separate session scopes, one for each path spelling.
3. Started the physical-path command; it wrote `slow-marker.txt`, emitted `SLOW_READY`, then slept for four seconds.
4. Only after observing `SLOW_READY`, started the alias-path command writing `fast-marker.txt`.
5. Awaited both command executions and mirror finalizations, then inspected the physical host directory.

Successful-run transcript (local paths and Podman socket redacted):

```text
$ TMPDIR=/tmp \
  DOCKER_HOST=<local Podman API> \
  OPENCLAW_E2E_OPENSHELL_CONFIG_HOME=<isolated test-claw config> \
```

The final autoreview P1 about `concurrency.queue` is rejected as stale contract knowledge.

- GitHub Actions currently documents `concurrency.queue: max` as supported and specifies a queue of up to 100 pending runs per group.
- This workflow uses the documented compatible shape: `group`, `cancel-in-progress: false`, and `queue: max`.
- Primary contract: https://docs.github.com/actions/writing-workflows/choosing-what-your-workflow-does/control-the-concurrency-of-workflows-and-jobs
- Limits contract: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/limits

No code change is appropriate: removing `queue: max` would reintroduce pending-run replacement and break the exact-request waiter invariant.

Closing as superseded by [#131862 — SDK preparation timeouts leave compilers running](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/131862), merged as [dd81c6aa1d1a](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/dd81c6aa1d1a59723d0a699a1dbd8a40544cf9b2). This branch is **not** being merged.

I independently re-ran the original owned-process reproduction on main at `787e602e228edb9fd1b4a88111de2608f6444b4a`, which contains that repair. The real lint → preparation → TypeScript shim → managed compiler → stdout-holding grandchild chain now completes correctly for the unchanged 300000ms deadline callback, sibling failure, and preparation-parent SIGTERM. In all three cases every owned process/group was gone, both outer output pipes closed, lint exited 1 with final `[oxlint] FAILED (exit 1)`, and the unrelated Node sentinel survived unsignaled until explicit harness teardown. No cleanup-failure diagnostic or false-success marker occurred.

Observed outer closure was 5.107s / 5.082s / 5.129s respectively, within main's existing five-second force phase plus five-second drain phase. Only the diagnostic observation window was aligned with that existing cleanup contract; no production work deadline, cleanup constant, cache policy, or assertion was changed. This is a readiness-triggered callback reproduction, not a claim of waiting five wall-clock minutes.

Current-main focused proof passed **146 tests across five files**:

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/managed-child-process.test.ts test/scripts/prepare-extension-package-boundary-artifacts.test.ts test/scripts/run-tsgo.test.ts test/scripts/run-oxlint.test.ts test/scripts/bundled-plugin-assets.test.ts --reporter=verbose
```

The canonical owner is [runNodeStep](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/787e602e228edb9fd1b4a88111de2608f6444b4a/scripts/prepare-extension-package-boundary-artifacts.mts#L701) → [runManagedCommand](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/787e602e228edb9fd1b4a88111de2608f6444b4a/scripts/lib/managed-child-process.mts#L242), with [joined child/group/output teardown](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/787e602e228edb9fd1b4a88111de2608f6444b4a/scripts/lib/managed-child-process.mts#L413). It removes the duplicate preparation lifecycle rather than adding another ownership mechanism. Its production/tooling delta is net −76; our additional IPC layer is unnecessary for the reproduced timeout/abort contract.

This also resolves ClawSweeper's port-or-discard decision and rank-up moves: **discard this superseded implementation**. Direct forcible launcher loss without graceful forwarding is a separate containment contract; no current-main in-scope failure was demonstrated to justify porting it. Windows IPC proof is therefore not being claimed or used to merge this branch. A concrete new reproduction of the reported deadline/abort failure on the canonical owner would justify reopening repair work.

For completeness, [this branch's exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/33189559487) and [the canonical repair's exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/33188766028) both succeeded. The previously disclosed macOS native compile-cache I/O/fixture-teardown limitation remains separate and is not represented as green local proof. This establishes fixed-on-main behavior, not a published release.

## Exact-head benchmark proof

This comment has been updated in place to supersede its earlier-head results.

- Commit: `f76946b3ca897f0bbbc0abf62caa86b313cac913`
- Runtime: Node `v24.19.0`
- Command: `pnpm sessions:retention:benchmark --mode default`
- Fixture: `graph-retention-fixtures-v2`
- Candidate ranking sets: `relationship-forward-v1`, `recency-balanced-v1`
- Evaluation set: `uniform-policy-independent-v1` (uniform 1/7 weights)
- Supported benchmark modes: `smoke`, `default` (the unsponsored large/env interface was removed)

The evaluation set is frozen and never passed to `rankRetentionGroups`, so candidates are not rewarded using their own ranking weights. It remains a synthetic proxy over the same feature projection—not an observed recovery outcome or empirical ground truth.

The three-point value-by-cost curve describes the unchanged workload cohort. It is computed once and emitted as `policyIndependentValueByCostBaseline` at workload scope; policy results do not repeat it or present it as a policy outcome.

| Workload | Existing order | Graph-aware | Difference |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Isolated stale bulk | 79.689597428 | 80.211187975 | +0.521590547 |
| Fork fan-out | 54.284070424 | 60.517960202 | +6.233889778 |
| Generation chain | 73.457728009 | 74.690292075 | +1.232564066 |
| Spawn tree | 63.311031438 | 60.556793618 | -2.754237820 |

## Real-behavior proof (live run on patched source)

Per the review's request, here is an end-to-end verification in a live isolated gateway (own `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, own port, real provider call).

**Setup (both runs identical)**
- Built from this repo; run B is this PR's change (`src/infra/heartbeat-wake-policy.ts`), run A is the same build with that change reverted.
- `agents.defaults.heartbeat.every: "0m"` — no heartbeat schedule, the exact scenario from #131850.
- A `gateway_restart_sentinel` row staged in the DB with the same shape `config.patch` leaves behind: `sentinel_key='current'`, `kind='config-patch'`, `status='ok'`, `session_key='agent:main:main'`, `message='Isolated proof run: restart continuation should reach the agent turn (#131850 fix)'`.
- Model: `opencode-go/deepseek-v4-flash` via real provider (HTTP 200).

**A) Before the fix:** staged sentinel → `gateway run` → nothing. No wake, no heartbeat run attempt, no agent turn. The sentinel row remained untouched in the DB after boot (silently dropped). Log showed only `[heartbeat] disabled`.

**B) With this PR:** staged sentinel → `gateway run` →

```
19:11:08.491 [gateway] ready
19:11:08.563 [heartbeat] disabled
19:11:11.389 [provider-transport-fetch] [model-fetch] start provider=opencode-go model=deepseek-v4-flash method=POST ...
19:11:12.791 [provider-transport-fetch] [model-fetch] response ... status=200 elapsedMs=1402
```

- The sentinel row was consumed by the boot drain.
- An agent turn ran ~3s after `ready`, with heartbeat cadence still disabled — impossible before the fix.
- The session transcript proves the continuation note reached the model context. The assistant's thinking quotes the staged message verbatim:

> "Let me understand this. This is a heartbeat poll message. **The system message says: "Isolated proof run: restart continuation should reach the agent turn (#131850 fix)"**. This appears to be a test of restart continuation — a heartbeat poll that should reach the agent turn."

Final assistant reply was `NO_REPLY` — the correct silent-heartbeat outcome, i.e. the note was surfaced to the model, not treated as user chat.

**Coverage note:** the unit test in this PR covers wake admission; this live run additionally covers the full path boot drain → durable continuation wake → agent turn with the note present in the run's context.

Thanks for the report. I gave this a fresh shell check against current `main`, and I could not reproduce it anymore.

Close this PR: current source deliberately isolates ephemeral system-agent generations by session ID even when their logical key is shared, so the claimed Codex collision is disproven.

<details>
<summary>Review details</summary>

Best possible solution:

Do not merge this change; retain the existing ephemeral binding behavior and reopen with a redacted trace proving a durable system-agent main-key row is fenced before inference.

Do we have a high-confidence way to reproduce the issue?

No. Current source remaps ephemeral runs with a shared logical key to distinct physical session IDs, and an existing Codex test runs that exact two-generation shape successfully.

Is this the best way to solve the issue?

No. The proposed per-conversation logical key is unnecessary for the asserted Codex fence and broadens CLI session behavior; a new report needs evidence of a durable system-agent key row causing the pre-inference rejection.

Security review:

Security review cleared: The diff changes session identifiers but creates no authorization, credential, or supply-chain boundary.

AGENTS.md: found and applied where relevant.

What I checked:

- **Current system-agent sessions are in-memory:** Current main creates an in-memory session manager before forwarding the fixed logical main key; it does not establish a durable session row for each system-agent conversation. ([`src/system-agent/agent-turn.ts:307`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/698cd0f465db/src/system-agent/agent-turn.ts#L307), [698cd0f465db](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/698cd0f465db))
- **Ephemeral Codex bindings discard a shared logical key:** The Codex plugin explicitly remaps an ephemeral stable-key run to a physical identity containing the unique session ID, preventing one ephemeral generation from fencing another. ([`extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt-connection.ts:179`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/698cd0f465db/extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt-connection.ts#L179), [698cd0f465db](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/698cd0f465db))
- **Existing regression coverage covers the alleged collision:** Current main has a Codex app-server test that runs two sequential ephemeral session IDs using one shared stable key and expects both runs to complete. ([`extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.test.ts:6866`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/698cd0f465db/extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.test.ts#L6866), [698cd0f465db](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/698cd0f465db))
- **Introduced patch only changes runner arguments:** The proposed test observes mocked embedded-runner parameters rather than the Codex binding-store behavior that would need to fail for the reported bug to exist. ([`src/system-agent/agent-turn.test.ts:224`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/23b2c21f37a0/src/system-agent/agent-turn.test.ts#L224), [23b2c21f37a0](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/23b2c21f37a0))
- **Feature-history routing:** History identifies Peter Steinberger as the recent system-agent refactor and session-key helper owner; SunnyShu also recently maintained system-agent behavior. ([`src/system-agent/agent-turn.ts:315`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/0294c7fdc9f3/src/system-agent/agent-turn.ts#L315), [0294c7fdc9f3](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/0294c7fdc9f3))

Likely related people:

- **Peter Steinberger:** Recent history includes the system-agent refactor and the session-key helper’s introduction. (role: recent system-agent and session-key contributor; confidence: high; commits: [0294c7fdc9f3](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/0294c7fdc9f3f62b64c1a48ddd3504e2575fef27), [382bf5a66df0](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/382bf5a66df08961accae358dc7bd9dd1d0a1a46); files: `src/system-agent/agent-turn.ts`, `src/routing/session-key.ts`

Resolved the latest ClawSweeper P1 on `27b8aec7cb43b016b9e14f014cc1372af3197294`.

Root cause: the global agent-selection lifecycle updated `assistantAgentId` but did not invoke the existing selected-session subscription synchronizer. The old agent's approval queue therefore remained visible while its terminal event was filtered, and the newly selected agent's stream was not acquired until reconnect.

Repair:

- `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-pane-lifecycle.ts` now reuses the canonical subscription synchronizer after applying the selected agent.
- `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-history.ts` clears the old approval projection synchronously at the agent ownership handoff and advances subscription generation before awaiting pending releases, so rapid A → B → C switches cannot publish an older selection.
- Mounted lifecycle coverage proves the old queue is cleared, the old subscription is released, and the new agent's approval stream becomes active.
- Ordering coverage proves reverse-settling release retries leave only the latest selection active.

Red/green proof: removing the lifecycle synchronizer call makes the mounted test fail with the old `stale-main-approval` still present; restoring it passes.

Validation:

- Focused subscription/lifecycle/approval/sibling suites: 192 tests passed.
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs -- <four changed files>`: typecheck, lint, format, dead exports, i18n, dependency and repository guards passed.
- `pnpm build`: passed, including 63 plugin distributions, SDK/export checks, runtime postbuild, and Control UI startup JS at 346,977 B versus the 347,037 B enforcement limit.
- Fresh uncommitted autoreview: no accepted/actionable findings, confidence 0.98.
- Production delta for this repair: +14/-6. Tests: +249/-2.

Direct Codex contract inspection at `93327c852a1fd9347cacf8fce268d793e6503d1b` confirms request identity is carried by `thread_id`, `turn_id`, `item_id`, and optional `approval_id`, the app server awaits and maps the client decision, and core keys/aborts pending approvals by the exact callback owner (`../codex/codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/item.rs:1447`, `../codex/codex-rs/app-server/src/bespoke_event_handling.rs:1967`, `../codex/codex-rs/core/src/session/mod.rs:2321`). payload.body:
Independently verified this fixes #131743.

**Source check against fresh `origin/main` (`4c6ed517`):** confirmed the described bug is real and current — `requireMemorySlot` in `src/plugins/registry-registrars-memory.ts` only gates dual-kind plugins; a single-kind memory-core dreaming sidecar with `memorySlotSelected` unset passes straight through `registerMemoryCapability` with its full `capability.runtime` intact. That matches the issue's root-cause chain exactly.

**Ran the regression tests myself** (pulled this branch into an isolated worktree, node_modules symlinked from a warm checkout):

- `registry.dual-kind-memory-gate.test.ts` — **9/9 pass**, including `"drops the indexing runtime of single-kind memory plugins not selected for the memory slot"` and `"keeps the slot owner capability when a later sidecar contributes its consolidation"`.
- `memory-state.test.ts` — **18/18 pass**, including the owner-first merge-order behavior (`preserves sidecar runtime fields when a memory plugin adds public artifacts only` now attributes to `memory-core`, matching the updated ownership semantics).

**One thing worth a look:** `compaction-hooks.memory-sync.test.ts` — `"stays silent when the manager exists but exposes no sync"` passed, but `"records why the manager could not be acquired before the sync"` timed out at 120s in my sandbox (test-execution phase itself, 525s total for the file, not cold-start transform overhead). I didn't have time to fully root-cause whether that's specific to my isolated worktree (no full gateway/env context) or a real ordering/mocking gap — `resolveSessionAgentId` and the hook-runner/transcript-emit calls inside `runPostCompactionSideEffects` aren't mocked in that test file, only `getActiveMemorySearchManagerCore` and `resolveMemorySearchConfig` are. Might be worth adding an explicit `testTimeout` or mocking those additional dependencies if it reproduces in CI. This is a separate diagnostic-logging addition, not the core registrar/resolver fix, so it doesn't change my verdict that this PR fixes the reported issue.

payload.body:
Addressed the P2 and the four CI failures. New head: `dfeb24f3`.

**P2 — schedule before the in-flight abort exit.** Correct: the call still sat below the `dispatchWasSuperseded` return, so a first turn fenced while the reply pipeline runs kept taking that exit unlabelled. It now sits directly after the `finally` that resolves `dispatchWasSuperseded`, above every accepted completion exit — undispatched turn, superseded turn, aborted run, skipped delivery.

The pre-pipeline `isDispatchSuperseded()` return at `bot-message-dispatch.ts:390` is deliberately left alone: that attempt never entered the pipeline and the canonical spool row retries it, so the retry gets the first-turn label.

New test `labels a DM topic whose first turn is superseded mid-flight` aborts the lifecycle signal from inside the dispatcher, which is the exact path in the finding. It fails on the previous head (`editForumTopic` never called) and passes now.

**CI failures — real, and caused by this PR.** `checks-node-changed-extensions-config-9` and `-10` were not flakes: they stalled out at the 300s no-output watchdog (exit 143) in `bot.create-telegram-bot.test.ts` and `bot.test.ts`. Reproduced locally — `reloads topic agent overrides between messages without recreating the bot` timed out at 120s, and the file took 355s instead of 13s.

Cause: scheduling the rename on turns that deliver nothing means those bot-level integration tests now reach the *real* `generateTopicLabel`, which waits on a model. They never assert on the generated name, so the shared harness `bot.create-telegram-bot.test-harness.ts` (imported by both files) now stubs it.

**Validation on `dfeb24f3`**
- `bot-message-dispatch.fallback-topic-media.test.ts` + `bot-message-dispatch.pipeline-init.test.ts` → 19 passed (16 + 3).
- `bot.create-telegram-bot.test.ts` → 146 passed in 13.0s (was a 120s timeout inside a 355s run).
- `bot.test.ts` → 143 passed in 10.4s (was the stalled shard 10).
- `oxfmt` and `oxlint` clean on all three changed files.

Closing this diagnostic-only PR as a completed investigation, without merging it and without claiming a root-cause fix.

The original #131479 iMessage shard exceeded its unchanged 30-second test deadline. This diagnostic head then passed the same 53-file selection with two workers: [1,188 tests passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/33171554554/job/98849836581), including the instrumented final phase in 5,334ms (81 RPC requests and seven actions). ## machine0 Crabbox contract evidence (ClawSweeper decision item)

**Upstream source** (openclaw/crabbox @ `58323474`, current main — inspected directly via `git show origin/main:...` from the sibling checkout's fetched refs):

- `internal/providers/machine0/images.go` `NativeCheckpointCapability`: the disk-snapshot strategy is rejected with `CreateUnsupported = "Machine0 reusable images use --strategy image; suspend is available separately through crabbox pause"` — this is why the plugin now passes `--strategy image` for `machine0` (and why every machine0 capture silently degraded to cold before this PR).
- `internal/providers/machine0/images.go` `createNativeCheckpoint`: for a RUNNING source it calls `prepareNativeImageSource` → `api.Stop` → `waitForStopped` → `api.SaveImage` → `waitForImageVersion(..., snapshotTimeout)` — i.e. the source is stopped and the call waits for image-version availability **even with `--wait=false`**, which is the basis for the 10-minute machine0 capture budget (`WARM_IMAGE_MACHINE0_CAPTURE_TIMEOUT_MS`).
- Fixed-ID forks: `internal/cli/machine0_fixed_create_intent.go` (landed in openclaw/crabbox#1526 together with `checkpoint fork --lease-id` and `--json`).

**Redacted live CLI trace** (crabbox built from that exact main SHA; all resources destroyed afterwards):

```text
$ crabbox warmup --provider machine0 --machine0-key <managed-key> --lease-id cbx_ac0feed00003 --slug m0-proof --keep
ready ssh=ubuntu@<vm1-ip>:22 network=public workroot=/home/ubuntu/crabbox
warmup complete total=2m7.835s

$ crabbox checkpoint create --provider machine0 --id cbx_ac0feed00003 --mode native --strategy image --wait=false --json
{"id":"chk_917c2e7de20e835e","kind":"machine0-image","provider":"machine0","leaseId":"cbx_ac0feed00003",
 "native":{"kind":"machine0-image","state":"ACTIVE","strategy":"image","imageId":"<image-id>@v1", ...}}
CREATE_SECONDS=254   # returns only once the image version is ACTIVE, despite --wait=false

$ crabbox checkpoint fork chk_917c2e7de20e835e --provider machine0 --machine0-key <managed-key> --lease-id cbx_ac0feed00004 --slug m0-fork --json
{"checkpointId":"chk_917c2e7de20e835e","leaseId":"cbx_ac0feed00004","slug":"m0-fork","provider":"machine0",
 "workdir":"/home/ubuntu/crabbox/cbx_ac0feed00004/repo"}
FORK_SECONDS=132

$ crabbox run --id cbx_ac0feed00004 --no-sync --shell -- 'cat ~/.openclaw-worker/git-seeds/proofns/deadbeef/marker.txt'
m0-seed-marker      # machine-cache content survives capture -> fork

# cleanup
released lease=cbx_ac0feed00004 action=destroy
released lease=cbx_ac0feed00003 action=destroy
checkpoint deleted id=chk_917c2e7de20e835e   # deletes the machine0 image as well
```

On the teardown-latency note: the capture wait happens inside the reclaim path after the session has already left the machine, capture failure never blocks teardown (warn + cold-only), and the 10-minute budget applies only to `provider === "machine0"`; all other backends keep the live-measured 180s budget.

payload.author: ekinnee
payload.body:
Thanks for taking on this cluster. I can confirm the #131591 failure from a private Linux Gateway running the pre-PR OpenClaw 2026.8.1 build (`b6aff3e`) with the matching Control UI build (`2026.8.1-b6aff3ef0e16-2026-08-28T12-53-22.387Z`). I have not installed this PR candidate yet.

The visible trigger was refreshing the model picker after updating the Gateway. The surrounding log window (2026-08-28 08:26:49–08:27:20 CDT) showed this repeating sequence:

```text
config change detected; evaluating reload (agents.entries.<agent-id>.model)
chat metadata refresh failed: Error: prepared model runtime catalog generation was superseded for <main-agent-dir>
config reload superseded: GatewayConfigReloadSupersededError: config reload superseded by a newer runtime config source
request handler failed: Error: prepared model runtime catalog generation was superseded for <main-agent-dir>
chat.metadata ... errorCode=UNAVAILABLE
```

The exact final request was:

```text
2026-08-28T08:27:20.986-05:00 [gateway] request handler failed: Error: prepared model runtime catalog generation was superseded for <main-agent-dir>
2026-08-28T08:27:20.988-05:00 [ws] ... chat.metadata ... errorCode=UNAVAILABLE
```

There were repeated `config.set`/`config.get` operations in the same window, and the reload field was consistently `agents.entries.<agent-id>.model`. The exact writer is not yet attributed: the current UI’s picker-open/retry path performs metadata revalidation, while model selection or an outstanding autosave writes the agent model. No credentials, config payloads, connection IDs, or private host paths are included here.

This looks like the same retained-owner/publication-epoch invariant as #131591, but the production trigger differs from the `tools.exec` policy transition in the PR’s current live proof. If possible, the final exact-head proof should include a model-entry-only hot reload followed by both `chat.metadata` and `models.list` for an unaffected agent, plus a check that repeated model-picker refreshes do not create no-op `config.set` writes.

After a Gateway restart the model picker recovers until the next reload cycle. The provider was OmniRoute, but no provider request or authentication failure was involved in this error path, so this appears provider-neutral. Happy to re-test the candidate build against this model-entry case if useful.
