payload.body:
Proof added, using an image built from this PR head rather than the placeholder transcript the
previous body contained. That was a fair catch: the earlier before/after came from a derived
image on top of the published tag, not from this Dockerfile.

Image built from `0e5f4089d`:

```
$ podman build -t openclaw-pr131710:0e5f4089d .
$ podman image inspect openclaw-pr131710:0e5f4089d --format '{{.Digest}} {{.Created}}'
sha256:92ae7255c7488268a4cf21e524ef3733b847f2c53d7759dc4856b123de316cab  2026-08-28T10:49:50Z
```

Build log, showing the changed apt list installing the package:

```
[6/6] STEP 5/39: RUN ... apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
      ca-certificates curl git hostname lsof openssh-client openssl procps python3 tini
Get:37 http://deb.debian.org/debian bookworm/main amd64 openssh-client amd64 1:9.2p1-2+deb12u10 [994 kB]
Setting up openssh-client (1:9.2p1-2+deb12u10) ...
```

`ssh` in the PR-head image:

```
$ podman run --rm --entrypoint ssh openclaw-pr131710:0e5f4089d -V
OpenSSH_9.2p1 Debian-2+deb12u10, OpenSSL 3.0.20 7 Apr 2026

$ podman run --rm --entrypoint sh openclaw-pr131710:0e5f4089d -c 'command -v ssh'
/usr/bin/ssh

$ podman run --rm --entrypoint sh openclaw-pr131710:0e5f4089d \
    -c "dpkg-query -W -f='${Package} ${Version} (${Installed-Size}KB)\n' openssh-client"
openssh-client 1:9.2p1-2+deb12u10 (5801KB)
```

Same check on the published image:

```
$ podman run --rm --entrypoint sh ghcr.io/openclaw/openclaw:2026.8.1-beta.3 \
    -c 'command -v ssh || echo "ssh: NOT FOUND"'
ssh: NOT FOUND
```

Executable startup, which is the mechanism this PR changes. `src/agents/sandbox/ssh.ts:849`
calls `spawn(sshExecutable, ...)` with the bare name `ssh`, so this runs that same spawn inside
each image:

```
--- published image ---
$ podman run --rm --entrypoint node ghcr.io/openclaw/openclaw:2026.8.1-beta.3 \
    -e 'require("child_process").spawn("ssh",["-V"],{stdio:"inherit"})
        .on("error",e=>console.log("spawn error:",e.code,"-",e.message))'
spawn error: ENOENT - spawn ssh ENOENT

--- PR-head image ---
$ podman run --rm --entrypoint node openclaw-pr131710:0e5f4089d \
    -e 'require("child_process").spawn("ssh",["-V"],{stdio:"inherit"})
        .on("error",e=>console.log("spawn error:",e.code,"-",e.message))
        .on("exit",c=>console.log("ssh exited",c))'
OpenSSH_9.2p1 Debian-2+deb12u10, OpenSSL 3.0.20 7 Apr 2026
ssh exited 0
```

The client executes rather than only resolving, reaching the network layer:

```
$ podman run --rm --entrypoint ssh openclaw-pr131710:0e5f4089d \
    -o BatchMode=yes -o ConnectTimeout=5 -p 2222 nobody@127.0.0.1 true
ssh: connect to host 127.0.0.1 port 2222: Connection refused
```

Scope, stated plainly rather than implied: this shows the `ssh` executable resolving and running
inside the PR-head image, which is the `spawn ssh ENOENT` failure the change addresses. It is
not a full agent-driven sandbox session, which would additionally need a reachable SSH target
and a configured model provider. If that specific lane is wanted before merge, say so and I will
stand one up.

On size, the number in the body is measured by adding only this package to the published image,
so the two differ by one apt layer: 1452453516 -> 1460057262 bytes, a delta of 7603746 bytes
(7.60MB, 0.52%). I am deliberately not comparing the locally built PR-head image against the
published image, because a default local build and a published release build select different
bundled extensions and their absolute sizes are not comparable.

The PR body has been updated with the same evidence.

AI-assisted

I ran the compatibility case against the published `openclaw@2026.5.28` package, in addition to the current-Gateway run.

The PR head connected to the released Gateway over loopback through a real stdio MCP child. The Gateway negotiated protocol 4 and did not advertise `chat.message.get`. The proxy recorded only these Gateway requests:

```json
{"gatewayProtocol":4,"gatewayAdvertisesExactLookup":false,"rpcMethods":["connect","sessions.subscribe","sessions.get"],"exactLookupCalls":0,"boundedHistoryCalls":2,"attachmentFetchIsError":false,"attachmentCount":1}
```

The target was inside the legacy history window, so the fallback returned its attachment without probing the unsupported method. Against the current Gateway, the same PR head used one `chat.message.get` call and returned an attachment whose message was outside the 200-row history window.

This directly exercises the compatibility boundary described in the PR. The release source also shows [protocol v4](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e93216080aa1f425d3ab127014603eba8e365b2d/packages/gateway-protocol/src/version.ts#L1-L3), [hello method advertisement](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e93216080aa1f425d3ab127014603eba8e365b2d/src/gateway/server/ws-connection/message-handler.ts#L1828-L1836), and the [absence of `chat.message.get`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e93216080aa1f425d3ab127014603eba8e365b2d/src/gateway/methods/core-descriptors.ts#L189-L210).

After-fix proof from a real setup (per the rank-up move), plus attribution for the failed ClawSweeper live verification.

## Live-gateway proof (real setup)

Isolated dev gateway built from this branch (`OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` scratch dir, own port, dist-backed CLI + served Control UI, build stamp `7bd26fc722ad`), driven through the real dashboard in Chromium. All four availability states exercised end to end:

**1. No credential configured (`missing-auth`)** — agent default `anthropic/claude-fable-5`, empty auth store:

```
$ openclaw gateway call models.list --params '{"agentId":"main"}'
{"id":"claude-fable-5","available":false,"unavailableReason":"missing-auth"}
```

Composer disabled with "No provider credential is configured for this model. Set it up in Model Setup." and the working setup link.

**2. Genuine provider rejection (`auth-failed`)** — deliberately invalid Anthropic API key, rejected live by the provider during catalog discovery:

```
{"id":"claude-fable-5","available":false,"unavailableReason":"auth-failed"}
```

Composer disabled with the existing "Authentication failed…" copy — now only shown when it is true. A subsequently scripted stats cooldown did **not** override the live rejection (presence isn't acceptance).

**3. Transient cooldown (`cooldown`)** — recorded through the production failure writer (`markAuthProfileFailure`, reason `rate_limit`; log: `auth profile failure state updated: … reason=rate_limit window=cooldown`):

```
{"id":"grok-4","available":false,"unavailableReason":"cooldown","unavailableUntil":1787907366124}
```

Composer stayed **enabled** with no banner; a real send dispatched against the provider and the transcript showed the visible run outcome (`HTTP 400: "Incorrect API key provided. You can obtain an API key from https://console.x.ai."`) — no dead composer, no false auth claim.

**4. Reason-less unknown** — native CLI runtime rows with an unread account stay `available:false` with no `unavailableReason` and do not block the composer:

```
{"reason":null,"count":7,"sample":"claude-cli/claude-opus-5"}
{"reason":"missing-auth","count":222,"sample":"anthropic/claude-fable-5"}
```

## ClawSweeper live-verification failure attribution

The review's live run crashed before executing any test: the sandbox's system Chromium aborted at startup (`SIGABRT` in `ProcessSingleton::NotifyOtherProcessOrCreate` — visible in the review's own output; every test shows as skipped `↓`). The same suite is green on this exact head in CI (`checks-ui-e2e` lanes, run 33159816632-series on `5d5398e`) and passes locally (`chat-composer-redesign.e2e.test.ts` 7/7, `control-ui-auth-transports.e2e.test.ts` 3/3 against a real gateway). The failure is environmental, not a proof gap in the change.

I independently confirmed the missing-event case with pinned Chromium 151.0.7922.34 and an isolated local HTTP server. A normal explicit fetch abort closed the captured HTTP response unfinished and produced Page, BrowserContext, and CDP failure events. Navigating the same page to `about:blank` also closed the exact response with `destroyed=true` and `writableFinished=false`, but produced none of those browser failure events during a 16-second observation window.

That distinguishes this from the delayed-callback interleaving covered by #131690, which I landed earlier. Its polling change is only a partial repair and does not supersede this PR. The exact-response observation here is the correct owner-boundary proof; it also retains the negative control that prevents an independent upstream deadline from masquerading as browser cancellation.

I also checked [Node 22.22.3's source](https://github.com/nodejs/node/blob/v22.22.3/lib/_http_server.js#L1112-L1119): the diagnostics payload is published before the real request handler, including its exact request and response objects. The installed Node 24 source has the same ordering.

I am taking this existing PR through the mechanical conflict refresh and normal native landing gates, preserving the HTTP-boundary repair rather than creating another replacement. No production change, timeout increase, or approval bypass is needed. Fresh exact-head CI remains required before merge.

**Maintainer follow-up:** ClawSweeper’s review is clean, but an independent local review found one additional authority window not covered by the current tests. After the dispatcher checks authority, environment creation may await installation preparation and provider queues before `provider.provision()` executes. A revocation during those waits could still permit allocation.

**Suggested fix:** Carry the authorization callback into the provider lifecycle and revalidate it inside the queued callback immediately before `provider.provision()`. Add a regression that revokes authority while preparation or queueing is paused and proves allocation does not occur.

The existing authorization callback now flows through environment creation and is rechecked inside the provider queue callback immediately before `provider.provision()`. That requirement is now satisfied: [CI run 33155897264, attempt 2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/33155897264/attempts/2) passed on this unchanged head. Attempt 1's ten primary failures were dependency-install setup failures, before their tests/type checks/SDK report; representative logs showed npm download timeouts. Only failed jobs were rerun. No source, dependency override, timeout, or assertion was changed to get green.

### Fresh compiled-runtime authorization proof

Five fresh isolated Gateways exercised the actual native plugin registration, trusted-proxy identity, role-policy ceiling, public SDK dispatch, and Gateway method authorization. **All 60 operation cases and five missing-identity HTTP 401 controls passed.** The fixture used ordinary write-default routes and explicitly declared trusted-operator routes, each with an absent scopes header and an explicit read-only header. No synthetic Gateway client, patched registry, or injected grants were used.

Observed no-header authorization (read / write / admin):

| Named-role ceiling | Ordinary route | Trusted-operator route |
|---|---|---|
| read only | deny / deny / deny | allow / deny / deny |
| empty | deny / deny / deny | deny / deny / deny |
| write only | allow / allow / deny | allow / allow / deny |
| admin only | allow / allow / deny | allow / allow / allow |
| roles disabled | allow / allow / deny | allow / allow / allow |

An explicit read header allowed only read for nonempty/disabled roles and allowed nothing for the empty role. Denied calls returned `FORBIDDEN / MISSING_SCOPE` with the exact scope. Authorized reads returned the real empty node list. Authorized write/admin probes reached the deliberately absent device's `UNAVAILABLE / PAIRING_CHANGED` fence, proving authorization admission, **not successful device execution**; no real device command was dispatched.

Build provenance: [runtime artifact 9679671023](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/33155897264/artifacts/9679671023), build commit [`677afaeed8eb39de3bec1cf691dc057189a7ab44`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/677afaeed8eb39de3bec1cf691dc057189a7ab44), whose parents include the exact PR head. The tar SHA-256 was `0f570d24d83592dd5d338b4fae5bcff3313bd91ad0f9b259f42aac7f42e1a7cc`. Archive containment and relative links were checked before installation; runtime, launcher, fixture and source identities were checked around each run.

### Local proof and limitations

The original 13 tests and expanded 19 characterization cases passed before production edits. A finite frozen-input comparison matched **4,362,955 cases / 8,653,205 API results**, including original denied-scope bytes, blanks/duplicates, implication and role-prefix boundaries. This is not an exhaustive claim over arbitrary JavaScript inputs. Fresh isolated Codex autoreview was clean at the configured **P0** threshold, not an all-priority audit.

**311 distinct selected cases have passing runs across 18 files.** Earlier Node 26 attempts timed out during Gateway ownership-suite startup, leaving seven cases unexercised. @clawsweeper re-review

Round 2 (head `e3d890f1f02`) addresses the P1 (**Avoid stranding full legacy source-sync namespaces**) by adopting the review's recommended resolution — sponsor atomic rekey:

**What changed**

- **New `rekey(key, nextKey, value)` on the plugin-state keyed store** (`src/plugin-state/`, +140/-4 production, additive and optional — existing operations unchanged). Key and value move in one slot-neutral transaction: capacity limits do not apply because the row count is unchanged, `created_at`/TTL survive the move (eviction orders by age), a live target is never overwritten (`"conflict"`), a vanished source with a live target still reports `"rekeyed"` so rerun passes stay idempotent, and self-rekey throws `PLUGIN_STATE_INVALID_INPUT`.
- **The legacy ownership migration rekeys through it** whenever the host store exposes `rekey`; the shipped SQLite store always does, so a full 20,000-row reject-new namespace now converges in **one doctor pass** — no spare slot needed, no retained-and-hidden rows, no delete-first kill window. The register-first path remains only as a fallback for host stores without `rekey` support.
- This restores the narrowly specified contract previously proposed in #122386 (now closed as superseded by this PR), exactly as the review's Decision-needed section recommended.

@clawsweeper re-review after addressing all three cycles of findings.

## Changes since last review

### Fix 1: Record serialization (from cycle 2)
The Python helper now reads ALL of stdin into memory (`payload = stdin_buffer.read()`) and does a single `write_all(fd, payload)` — one serialized write per record. Old code chunked into 64KB writes which could interleave across concurrent appenders.

### Fix 2: Separator logic moved inside append_atomic (from cycle 2)
The Python helper now computes the newline separator inside the same serialized operation: `os.pread` reads the last byte, prepends `\n` if needed, then writes the complete buffer. The TypeScript consumer no longer pre-reads or pre-computes separators.

### Fix 3: Provenance-before-commit ordering restored (from cycle 2)
`wrapToolMemoryFlushAppendOnlyWrite` now records provenance FIRST, then calls commit. If commit fails, the observer rolls back provenance. Old code committed first with a no-op provenance callback.

### Fix 4: TS/Python separator alignment (from cycle 3)
Removed the `!content.startsWith("\n")` guard from the TS separator estimate to match the Python helper's logic (which only checks the file's last byte).

### New: Regression tests (from SRE review)
5 new tests in `fs-bridge-mutation-helper.test.ts` covering:
- Append to empty file (no separator)
- Append to file ending with `\n` (no separator)
- Append to file not ending with `\n` (exactly one separator)
- Multiple sequential appends (correct note boundaries)
- Nested directory creation

### New: Signal warning (from SRE review)
Added JSDoc to `RemoteShellSandboxFsBridge.appendFile` documenting that callers MUST supply a bounded signal — Python helper blocks on `stdin.read()` without one.

## SRE verdict
The SRE engineer reviewed the full diff and gave **SHIP** with 3 pre-merge items (all addressed above). Key findings:
- Separator race (file ends with `\n`): residual, microsecond window, acceptable
- contentAfter staleness: acknowledged, diagnostic provenance only
- Test bridge gap: noted, production path uses Python helper

Addressed the review findings on the new head:

- **Escape the stored revoker label (P2 / security)** — fixed. `renderTerminalSafeTable` already strips C0/C1 controls from every cell (`packages/terminal-core/src/table.ts` → `sanitizeTerminalText`), so raw escape sequences could not reach the terminal even before this change — but silent stripping is weaker than the file's own convention of visible `\u{...}` escapes. - **Durable-authority policy (P1 merge risk)** — maintainer-decided, not an open question: the until-revoked default was chosen explicitly because shipped "Always allow" semantics are already indefinite, so changing the default would silently alter what existing operators believe they granted. `tools.exec.grantExpiryDays` gives enterprises time-bounded defaults for **new** grants only; terms freeze at mint. The prior fixed-30-day shape never shipped (the grants table exists on no release tag), so the documented fail-closed lazy rebuild is upgrade-safe: pre-release dev databases rebuild the table on first mint, and there is nothing shipped to migrate. This is recorded in the PR body and `docs/tools/exec-approvals.md`.
- Also folded in this push: the two cross-lane inventory tests that first fail on full runs (`core-descriptors.since.test.ts` release-train roster now lists `exec.approval.grants.list`/`.revoke`; `root-command-descriptions.test.ts` classifies the `approvals grants` container), and a `stubGrants` typing fix in `approvals-page.test.ts`.

Closing this PR for now. The fix is complete and tested (RED→GREEN verified, 14/14 tests pass, tsgo/oxfmt/oxlint clean), but the fork this branch lives on is ~68k commits behind upstream and cannot be synced with the current token's OAuth scopes (no workflow scope, and syncing would update .github/workflows/ files).

The branch is based on the fork's stale main, which predates the introduction of src/infra/state-migrations.media-persistence.ts, so GitHub sees the files as conflicting adds rather than modifications.

The fix is ready to re-submit once the fork is synced. Branch: fix-media-source-safe-integer @ febef4f8. The change:
- CASTs the three SUM() aggregates in readMediaSourceVersion to TEXT in SQL (sidesteps DatabaseSync's RangeError on oversized INTEGERs)
- Parses the text as BigInt so drift comparison stays exact
- Adds a regression test with timestamps at 10^15 (SUM ~ 10^16 > Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER)

Fixes #130998 — will re-open once the fork is up to date.

[P2] Keep URL expansion for valid snapshots that have no refs

At head `316fc98f27224e850d6ab1b003f362b144bf6096`, the new condition in `extensions/browser/src/browser/pw-tools-core.snapshot.ts:348–351` treats an empty filtered ref map as a selector miss. This finalizer also handles snapshots without a selector. For example, `snapshot --depth 0 --urls` on a page with an unnamed `<main>` and a nested link keeps the root but filters out the link's ref; current main still appends the discovered URL, while this condition suppresses it. The same can happen for a matching selector with no ref-bearing content.

Please keep the shared finalizer's URL behavior and suppress collection only when the selector owner actually observed no matches. Add the valid ref-free/depth-zero URL case alongside the missing-selector regression. This is a source-derived finding against current main `c17d442a6e2121bf2f4edb5d6c1397d6e45cf84c`, not a live reproduction. The prior missing-selector/URL finding is addressed, but its current fix changes this separate valid-result path.

payload.author: steipete
payload.body:
Thanks @clawsweeper — no correctness findings and "land the focused shared build-identity repair" matches the intent here. Responding to each item before merge.

### Before merge 1: add real behavior proof

Applied. The live verification here failed for a harness reason, not a product one: the step waited 30s for `2 passed`, but this E2E builds the production Control UI **twice** (`buildProductionControlUiE2e` for build A in `beforeAll`, then build B mid-test), so it needs ~165s. The captured log stops at ` RUN v4.1.11`, before the first build finished.

Local run of the exact command's test target, on this head:

```
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  2 passed (2)
   Start at  18:49:44
   Duration  165.35s (transform 273ms, setup 432ms, import 3.01s, tests 123.60s, environment 0ms)

[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 182.53s
```

That is the production-browser E2E you identified as the covering proof — real Chromium, two real production bundles, a real service worker held in `install`, and a real Gateway reconnect.

The regression test was also verified to fail on pre-fix code for the intended reason, which is the part that proves the fix rather than the absence of the bug:

```
FAIL  ui/src/app/service-worker-refresh.runtime.test.ts > releases the reconnect fence
      when the replacement serves this document's build
AssertionError: expected true to be false
```

Its three sibling tests in that file pass both before and after, so it discriminates rather than over-fits.

Full `ui` unit lane on this head: 749 files, 11052 tests passed, 18 files / 67 tests skipped, 0 failures. `pnpm check:changed` exit 0. Codex autoreview on the diff: clean, no accepted findings.

### Before merge 2: resolve merge risk (P1), production net +41

Confirmed and intended. `git diff --numstat` against the merge base:

| File | + | - | Class |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| `ui/src/app/sw-refresh.runtime.ts` | 30 | 5 | source |
| `ui/src/build-info.ts` | 16 | 0 | source |
| `ui/src/main.ts` | 2 | 2 | source |
| `ui/src/app/service-worker-refresh.runtime.test.ts` | 96 | 48 | test |

Production net +41, tests net +48. About half the production growth is the two comments recording the ordering invariant (the worker announces its build inside `activate`, before reporting `activated`), which is the non-obvious fact a future reader needs.

On "should remain the only activation decision path" — it is, and that is the point of the change. `controlUiWorkerActivationRetires()` in `build-info.ts` is now the sole rule; `main.ts` reloads through it and `sw-refresh.runtime.ts` reads it. The bug existed precisely because two copies of that rule disagreed. No terminal-specific detector was added, per your recommended option 1.

This fix cannot be net-neutral: it introduces a signal the code never observed — which build the activating worker serves. `scriptURL` cannot supply it, because an update keeps the registering document's `?v=` while serving new bytes (the reason that assertion was dropped in #126584).

### Rank-up move: after-fix proof from a real setup

Applied above — terminal output from the real production-browser E2E on this head, plus the pre-fix failure of the regression test.

### Note on the live-verification step

The 30s `expect_output` window cannot pass for this file regardless of the code under review. Separately worth fixing: this E2E runs two full production Vite builds inside its own 120s test timeout, which also blew that timeout on a loaded machine during this investigation. Different defect from this PR, so I left it alone rather than widening scope.
